findings.evidence: Mutual Defense Assistance Act of 1949 and Mutual Security Act of 1951 (Statutes at Large); Devlin, Chief of Station, Congo (2007); Church Committee, Alleged Assassination Plots Involving Foreign Leaders (Nov 1975) on the Lumumba plot and the Sept 1960 Gottlieb toxin; Gordon testimony on Brazil 1962 election funding (Lincoln Gordon, Brazil's Second Chance, 2001); Roosevelt, Countercoup (1979) read against Wilber; Gasiorowski on Iran's client collapse, 'The 1953 Coup d'Etat in Iran', IJMES 19 (1987); Simpson, Economists with Guns (2008) on the US-Indonesian army relationship 1958-65.

findings.title: Alignment moved only inside windows: elections, successions, independence, economic collapse and defeat; outside a window money bought nothing
findings.detail: Every flip in the 1947-65 record sits on a discrete opening: Italy Apr 1948 (election), Yugoslavia Jun 1948 (Cominform split), China 1949-50 (civil-war end; the Sino-Soviet Treaty of 14 Feb 1950 came with a $300M credit at 1% over five years, the Soviet 'Marshall' calibration), Iran Aug 1953 (oil-boycott collapse), Guatemala Jun 1954 (army defection), Egypt 1955-56 (arms-deal and Aswan windows), Hungary Oct-Nov 1956 (succession and revolt), Syria 1957-58, Iraq Jul 1958, Guinea Sept 1958, Cuba 1959-61, Congo Jul 1960-Jan 1961 (independence 30 Jun 1960 and Katanga secession 11 Jul; Lumumba appealed to Moscow only after Belgian troops returned), Brazil 1964, Indonesia 1965, Ghana 1966. The 24 African independences of 1960 were each a window with a deadline, and the record shows the superpowers mostly lost them to a third party: the ex-metropole (French Community and CFA franc, 1958-60) and the Non-Aligned leaders themselves. The scripted timeline already produces these windows (Independence effects, leadership deaths, coups, elections implied by date triggers); the missing piece is that nothing lets a player pre-position before the window and nothing resolves the window from pre-positioned influence. Windows also give the decision budget its shape: 2-4 windows per game-month worldwide is close to the actual historical density in 1958-62.
findings.evidence: Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance, 14 Feb 1950 (credit terms in Goncharov, Lewis & Xue, Uncertain Partners, 1993); Kalb, The Congo Cables (1982); Westad, The Global Cold War (2005) chapters 4-5; Chafer, The End of Empire in French West Africa (2002) on the 1958 Community referendum; assets/data/scenario/1950/events/*.ron already dating 30+ of these windows.

findings.title: The five mechanisms history says matter most, in order
findings.detail: (1) SECURITY-ELITE CAPTURE: whoever equips and trains the army owns the coup option and the veto over the government line; economic aid consolidates but the army converts (Iran, Guatemala, Congo, Brazil, Indonesia; and the reverse cases Iraq 1958, Cuba 1959, Ethiopia 1974). (2) WINDOWS: alignment moves only at elections, successions, independences, defeats and economic collapses; money outside a window is stored, not spent. (3) THE AUCTION: non-aligned leaders actively bid one bloc against the other, so a rival's OFFER is the trigger for yours and a WITHDRAWAL is a crisis in itself; the non-aligned pole is a player, not a residue. (4) NATIONALIST BACKLASH: exposed sovereignty violations move alignment against the intervening side and raise the world-opinion price of the next one; the money cost of covert action was never the deterrent, the attribution was (Syria 1957, Indonesia 1958, Cuba 1961, U-2 1960, CCF exposure 1967). (5) FACTIONS AS THE STORE OF INFLUENCE: parties, unions, churches, officer corps and student bodies hold the influence that governments merely express (Italy's parishes and Civic Committees, Force Ouvriere split of Dec 1947 with AFL money, the PCI's Moscow subsidy, Lumumba University alumni); a country with an Eastern-armed army, a non-aligned president and a jailed communist party (Egypt 1959) is the normal case, not the edge case, and cannot be represented by one enum. A sixth, lesser but real: LEGIBILITY OF AID, where a named dam or steel plant with a flag on it bought more lean per dollar than any balance-of-payments loan (Aswan, Bhilai, Volta, Salang tunnel 1964, versus the Helmand Valley failure).
findings.evidence: Synthesis of the sources above; Westad, The Global Cold War (2005) for the structural argument; O'Rourke (2018) and Levin (2020) for the quantitative floors; Carew, 'The American Labor Movement in Fizzland: The Free Trade Union Committee and the CIA', Labor History 39 (1998) on Force Ouvriere; Cullather, The Hungry World (2010) on Helmand.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Faction ledger under the government line (per-country: ARMY, GOVERNMENT/ruling coalition, MASS ORGANIZATIONS as one 'street' faction, plus a LEADER bond), keeping the existing three-valued Alignment as the derived government line
mechanics_recommendations.why: Egypt 1955-72, Indonesia 1958-65, Guinea 1958-62 and Ghana 1957-66 all had an Eastern-armed army, a non-aligned leader and a persecuted communist party at once; a single enum cannot hold them, and covert ops need a target smaller than a country. The record shows the army faction owns coups, the government faction owns treaties and bids, the street faction owns elections and uprisings. Three factions plus a leader stays inside the dossier-card budget; church/unions/students are texture inside the street faction.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Each faction carries a signed lean (West/East) in a narrow integer scale, a patron tag for the army (whose equipment lineage it runs on), and a visibility flag. The government line (the enum every existing system reads through Military::alignment_of) is recomputed only at windows from the factions that resolve that window (election: street plus government; coup: army; independence: leader plus army). Read by the player as one dossier card in the same register as the intel cards: 'EGYPT - GOVT: NON-ALIGNED (NASSER) / ARMY: EAST-EQUIPPED, CZECH ARMS 1955 / STREET: NATIONALIST, COMMUNISTS JAILED / NEXT WINDOW: NONE SCHEDULED'. Decision it changes: which verb has any purchase here at all (arms to the army vs money to a party vs a bid to the leader), and whether a coup is even on the menu.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Bids: the aid verb as a named, priced offer with an announcement shock, a delivery clock and a withdrawal that is itself a crisis pretext; rival bids visible through political intel
mechanics_recommendations.why: Every historical aid effect landed at announcement (Czech arms Sept 1955, Soviet Aswan credit Oct 1958, Guinea Aug 1959) or at withdrawal (Aswan 19 Jul 1956 to Canal nationalization 26 Jul), and the non-aligned leaders' actual play was to show one bloc's offer to the other. The economic-agency research already reserved 'contested foreign bids / the Aswan auction' as the best post-v1 fusion of pillars 2-4, and the Great Project machinery exists.
mechanics_recommendations.how: A bid names a recipient, a faction it lands on (a dam lands on GOVERNMENT and LEADER, an arms tranche on ARMY, PL-480 grain on STREET), a stock cost drawn from the real budget (Marshall-scale aid competes with guns and butter; covert money does not), a term, and a legibility class (showpiece vs balance-of-payments) that sets the lean-per-stock rate. On acceptance the recipient's faction lean shifts at once by the announcement value and the delivery clock starts; the rival superpower gets an intel-fuzzed wire line ('CAIRO REPORTED WEIGHING A SOVIET OFFER') and a counter-bid window. Withdrawal is a command that refunds undelivered stock, moves the lean the other way by more than the announcement gave, and banks a grievance the timeline's crisis triggers can read. Read as a STANDING BIDS list on the dossier and a monthly newspaper line; the decision it changes is outbid, hold, or withdraw, and for a non-aligned player, which bid to accept and which to leak.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Windows as the only moments the government line moves: elections on a sourced calendar, successions and coups from the timeline, independence events, economic-collapse and defeat triggers; each window has a lead time during which pre-positioned faction lean is what resolves it
mechanics_recommendations.why: Alignment never moved outside a window in 1947-65, and the actual world density of windows (2-4 per month in 1958-62) matches the decision budget house rule; this also converts the 37 scripted independences and the timeline's coups from railroad into contest without touching the event grammar.
mechanics_recommendations.how: A window object (country, kind, resolve date, resolving factions) is scheduled either by an election calendar data file (Turkey 14 May 1950, UK 23 Feb 1950, Italy 7 Jun 1953, W. Germany 6 Sept 1953, India 1951-52, Chile 4 Sept 1964, and so on, sourced) or by existing events (Independence, AdjustStability below a floor, war defeat, leader death). From lead-time start it appears in a THE COLONIAL QUESTION / ELECTIONS AHEAD newspaper section and on the dossier with an outcome ladder (PROBABLE / POSSIBLE / UNLIKELY per government line) computed from visible faction leans. At resolution the government line is set from the resolving factions plus a seeded roll from a b"windows" stream, then SetAlignment-style downstream effects fire. Scripted events keep their options but their SetAlignment effects become a lean push on a faction rather than an override, unless the content author marks them as historical hard facts. The decision it changes: what to spend and where in the months before a date the player can see.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Covert flip operations (party funding, election interference, coup sponsorship) that consume the espionage layer's network and outcome ladder, gated on faction state not cash, with nationalist backlash as the PROVEN-attribution branch
mechanics_recommendations.why: Iran cost $285K and Guatemala $2.7M; cash was never the constraint. Success depended on army lean and an ongoing crisis; every exposed failure (Syria 1957, Indonesia 1958, Cuba 1961) moved the target against the intervening side and gave the rival propaganda. Levin's +3 points for election ops sets the ceiling for interference, and the espionage doc already reserves coup sponsorship and party funding as influence-pillar ops on its ladder.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Election interference: a network spend that adds a bounded push (calibrated to about three points of the resolving window's margin) to the street or government faction ahead of a scheduled election, exposure clock as for any op, PROVEN attribution flips the push negative and hands the rival a world-opinion gain. Coup sponsorship: only offered when ARMY lean favors the sponsor and stability is below a threshold; outcome ladder branches are CLEAN (line flips, legitimacy loss small), SUCCESS-WITH-EVIDENCE (flips, grievance banked, rival propaganda), QUIET FAILURE (network spent), LOUD FAILURE (target line moves against sponsor, tension spike, deniability spent; Syria/Cuba). Supporting a low-stability client also seeds a 'successor lean' against the patron, so an unstable client is a visible liability on the dossier. Read through the existing PUBLIC WIRE / INTERNAL CABLE registers; decision changed: whether to gamble a window on a coup versus waiting for the next election with a bid.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: World opinion as a bounded global pool with per-bloc sign, fed by coercion (crackdowns, exposed ops, colonial wars) and spent by the Non-Aligned pole as prestige; propaganda programs are multipliers on the price the other side pays, not alignment movers
mechanics_recommendations.why: Hungary and Suez in one fortnight (Nov 1956) cost each side its moral case with the other side's public and the Third World simultaneously; RFE and the peace campaigns changed beliefs slowly and never flipped a government, but they set the price of every crackdown. Bandung (Apr 1955) and Belgrade (Sept 1961) show the non-aligned converting superpower misconduct into their own standing.
mechanics_recommendations.how: A single signed integer per bloc (West opinion, East opinion) in tenths like Tension, decremented by named acts (CrushUprising command, PROVEN blown ops, colonial war months, nuclear tests after 1954) and slowly recovering. Standing propaganda programs (radio, cultural, student scholarships) are funding tiers with no upkeep micro that multiply the opinion loss the RIVAL takes per act and give a small monthly drift to street factions in listening countries; a Hungary-style event can also turn a broadcast program into a blowback event. Non-aligned countries gain prestige from opinion swings and from hosting conferences, and prestige is what lets them extract larger bids and what the victory checkpoint scores for them. Read in the newspaper's WORLD IN NUMBERS as 'WORLD OPINION: WEST -12 THIS MONTH (BUDAPEST)'. Decision changed: whether to crush a satellite uprising now (bloc holds, opinion falls, rival's propaganda multiplier bites) or let it drift toward a Finland-style settlement.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Bloc discipline and the mirror: satellites and allies carry the same faction ledger, drift is visible, and the superpower's verbs against its own bloc (subsidy, crackdown, Finlandization treaty, ClientState clause) write to it
mechanics_recommendations.why: Yugoslavia 1948, Albania 1961, Romania 1964, Iceland 1956, Ceylon 1956, Iraq 1959, Japan 1960 and de Gaulle's France all show alliance members' politics moving on their own; the war-termination doc left ClientState and Neutralization clauses without teeth precisely for this pillar.
mechanics_recommendations.how: No new object: a bloc member's government and street factions drift monthly from occupation/garrison presence, unpopular basing, economic transfers (Soviet post-1956 credits to Poland and Hungary as a Bid), and rival propaganda. A member whose government line would resolve away from the bloc at its next window raises a dossier warning; the superpower chooses subsidy (a Bid), a Finlandization-style treaty (fixes the line at Non-Aligned with a standing veto and opinion cost near zero, Austria 1955 / Finland 1948 calibration), or a crackdown (holds the line, pays world opinion, feeds the rival multiplier). ClientState treaty clauses set the army patron and government line directly; Neutralization sets the line to Non-Aligned and locks it for the truce term. Read as the same dossier card; decision changed: how much of the budget goes to keeping the bloc versus contesting the frontier.

pitfalls: Aid as a money-to-alignment slider. Marshall money went to countries already Western; Soviet money to Egypt, Indonesia, Ghana, Guinea, Somalia and Sudan all ended in expulsions; the effect lives in announcements and withdrawals on named projects, and in what the recipient's army runs on. If lean accrues linearly per dollar the USSR player can never compete (1/10th the budget) and the US player wins Africa by spreadsheet.

Coups priced in cash with a success percentage. Iran cost $285,000 and nearly failed on day one; Cuba cost $46M and failed completely. Gate coups on visible local facts (army lean, stability, a live crisis) and show the outcome ladder; a cash-scaled probability teaches exactly the wrong lesson and contradicts the espionage house rules.

Ignoring the backlash branch. Syria 1957, Indonesia 1958, Cuba 1961, Guinea's treatment by Eisenhower in 1958 and Lumumba's death all moved alignment AGAINST the acting power. If a failed or exposed op merely costs tension and a network, covert action becomes strictly dominant and the sim loses the reason the historical actors hesitated.

Non-Aligned as a passive middle. Nasser, Nehru, Tito, Sukarno, Nkrumah and Toure were the most active players on the board and their auction is where most superpower money went; a residual state with no verbs turns the decolonization wave back into a script.

Per-country granularity only. The normal 1950s case (Eastern arms, non-aligned leader, jailed communists, Western food aid) has no representation in one enum, and covert ops cannot target anything smaller than the flag.

Letting influence decisions scale with 226 countries. Historically the superpowers concentrated on a handful of bidders at a time; use windows and a capped bid portfolio so the player sees 2-4 live contests per month, and let AI-vs-AI contests resolve from the same ledger silently.

Instant blowback. Iran's price came in 1979 and Guatemala's over 36 years; the sim needs a shorter fuse than history but not a same-month one: a banked grievance that the timeline's existing OptionChosen/EventFired chains and the successor-lean rule can cash years later, or the player never feels the long shadow that made the era's statesmen cautious.

Broadcasting as an alignment mover. RFE reached half of Poland and flipped nothing; if radio programs shift the government line the whole Eastern bloc decays on autopilot. Make them price multipliers and street-faction drift, and give them their own Hungary-shaped blowback event.
analysts.first_hour_test: Playing the USA from 1 Jan 1950, the player opens Turkey's dossier and sees a faction card (GOVT: WESTERN-LEANING, SEEKING NATO / ARMY: US-EQUIPPED, TRUMAN DOCTRINE 1947 / STREET: CONTESTED / NEXT WINDOW: GENERAL ELECTION 14 MAY 1950, PROBABLE: WESTERN) and can place one bid (a MAP tranche or grain) that visibly moves the ladder before the date; on 14 May the newspaper reports the Democrat Party landslide and Turkey's line is confirmed by the window, not by a scripted SetAlignment. In the same months the player sees Yugoslavia's drought appeal and the standing question of keeping Tito afloat (a bid that moves Yugoslavia toward Non-Aligned-but-Western-armed, denies Moscow, and is scored as a denial at the 1955 checkpoint), and reads the Stockholm Appeal (Mar 1950) as an Eastern propaganda program that lowers Western opinion in Italy and France's street factions while the French dockers refuse to unload US arms (Feb-Mar 1950). Playing the USSR the mirror holds: fund the peace campaign, subsidize the PCF's strike, watch the Sino-Soviet treaty (14 Feb 1950, $300M credit) land as a bid on the PRC card, and decide whether to punish or ignore Belgrade. The proof of playability is that by the North Korean crossing on 25 Jun 1950 the player has made 2-4 influence decisions, seen one window resolve from pre-positioned lean, seen one rival bid through intel, and can point to one country whose line or faction lean differs from the hands-off run because of what they did.

findings.title: The leader's formation and power base decided alignment more than the aid ledger did — model regime type and power base, not just a bloc tag
findings.detail: The nine leaders in the brief sort cleanly by where they got their power, and that predicted drift for a decade. Party-state builders who came up through mass parties or unions (Nkrumah's CPP, Sekou Toure's PDG via the CGT unions, Nyerere's TANU, Ben Bella via the FLN) treated non-alignment as regime legitimacy and were expensive for either bloc to move; metropole-groomed leaders (Houphouet-Boigny, a French deputy and minister 1956-59; Bourguiba, Paris-trained lawyer; Senghor) locked into the former metropole with defense agreements; leaders with no institutional base (Lumumba, an MNC that held ~a quarter of the 1960 seats, no army loyalty, 11 weeks in office) were toppled before any bid could pay out. Aid did not buy alignment on its own: the US financed Nkrumah's Volta dam (Kennedy approved the loans in Dec 1961) and Ghana still hosted Soviet advisers, went to Moscow, and voted against Washington at the UN; the USSR poured credits into Guinea in 1959-60 and was expelled (ambassador Solod, Dec 1961) when Toure decided the Soviets were a threat to his party. The lesson for UGS: a newborn state needs two attributes beside its three-valued Alignment — a regime type (party-state / parliamentary / military / traditional-monarchy) and a power base (party / army / metropole / traditional), because those govern (a) how much a bid moves alignment, (b) how sticky the result is, and (c) who can be couped.
findings.evidence: Westad, The Global Cold War (2005) ch. 3-4; Mazov, A Distant Front in the Cold War: The USSR in West Africa and the Congo 1956-1964 (2010) on Guinea/Ghana/Mali; Mahoney, JFK: Ordeal in Africa (1983) on Volta and Guinea; Legvold, Soviet Policy in West Africa (1970); Chafer, The End of Empire in French West Africa (2002) on Houphouet; Wikipedia 'Ahmed Sekou Toure' (Solod expulsion Dec 1961), 'Patrice Lumumba', 'Kwame Nkrumah'.

findings.title: The former metropole was the largest bidder and a distinct actor, with a residual veto that could be withdrawn — the French Community, the Commonwealth defense agreements, and Belgian abandonment are three different bidder profiles
findings.detail: France: the Sept 1958 Fifth Republic constitution (Title XII) created the Community; the 28 Sept 1958 referendum was in effect a bid (yes = Community, non = Guinea alone); the 1960-61 'accords de cooperation' with 12 ex-colonies bundled currency (CFA franc), aid, technical assistants, and in most cases defense agreements with garrisons (Dakar, Port-Bouet, Libreville, Fort-Lamy, Diego-Suarez); Foccart's Secretariat ran it. The residual was real: French paratroopers reversed the Gabon coup within 24 hours (18-19 Feb 1964, restoring Leon M'ba), and French troops stayed in Bizerte until 1963 over Bourguiba's objection (Bizerte crisis, July 1961, ~600 Tunisians killed). Britain: the Commonwealth (1949 London Declaration let republics stay), defense agreements (Anglo-Malayan Defence Agreement, Oct 1957; Kenya base rights), and intervention when asked — Royal Marines suppressed the Tanganyika Rifles mutiny (20-25 Jan 1964) and the Uganda and Kenya mutinies the same week, at Nyerere's request. Belgium: no bid at all — the 30-year van Bilsen plan (1955) collapsed into the Brussels Round Table (Jan-Feb 1960) setting 30 June 1960; the Force Publique had ~1,100 Belgian officers and zero Congolese; General Janssens's 'before independence = after independence' blackboard on 5 July triggered the mutiny, Belgian paratroopers landed on 10 July, Katanga seceded 11 July. Belgium is the 'withdrawn bidder' profile that opens a vacuum. And the metropole's interest often ran against its own bloc: Washington held its Guinea aid and ambassador until 1959 to avoid offending de Gaulle, abstained with the colonial powers on UN Res 1514, then broke with Portugal on Angola at the UN (March 1961) only to retreat when the Azores base lease came up (1962). Senator Kennedy's 2 July 1957 Algeria speech was a bid against France for the Arab world's future states.
findings.evidence: Chafer 2002; Bat, Le syndrome Foccart (2012); Wikipedia '1964 Gabonese coup d'etat', 'Bizerte crisis', 'Tanganyika Rifles mutiny', 'Anglo-Malayan Defence Agreement'; Nzongola-Ntalaja, The Congo from Leopold to Kabila (2002); Mahoney 1983 ch. on Portugal/Azores; Kennedy Senate speech 2 July 1957 (Congressional Record).

findings.title: The bidding window was real, short, and observable: recognition in days, aid packages in months, closed by regime consolidation in ~12-18 months
findings.detail: Recognition races: PRC recognized the DRV on 18 Jan 1950, the USSR on 30 Jan, and the US answered by recognizing Bao Dai's State of Vietnam on 7 Feb 1950 — the first bidding window in the game's first hour. The USSR recognized Guinea on 5 Oct 1958 (three days after independence) and had the first credits signed in 1959 (about 140m rubles), while the US ambassador arrived in mid-1959 and aid sat 'in committee'. Congo: independence 30 June 1960, mutiny 5 July, Katanga 11 July, UN Res 143 on 14 July, Lumumba's request for Soviet aircraft and trucks answered in August (Il-14s and ~100 trucks), Mobutu's coup 14 Sept — the entire window was eleven weeks. Package cadence: Ghana-USSR economic agreement (Aug 1960, ~$40m), Ghana-Volta (US/UK/World Bank/Kaiser, 1961-62), Indonesia's $100m US Ex-Im loan (Feb 1950) versus Soviet arms credits for West Irian (~$1bn, 1960-62), Egypt's Czech arms deal (27 Sept 1955) then the withdrawn US/UK Aswan offer (19 July 1956) then Soviet finance (1958). Structurally: Soviet credits to the developing world 1954-64 were ~$3.5-4bn and concentrated in a dozen states (India, Egypt, Afghanistan, Indonesia, Iraq, Ghana, Guinea, Mali, Ethiopia), i.e. Moscow bid hard on a few openings rather than spreading. Once the first cabinet, first army command, and first budget were in place the window closed: later movement required a coup, an election, or a leader's death.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia 'State of Vietnam', 'Democratic Republic of Vietnam' (recognition dates); Mazov 2010 (Guinea credits, Congo airlift); Goldman, Soviet Foreign Aid (1967) for the aggregate; Kahin & Kahin, Subversion as Foreign Policy (1995) for Indonesia; Wikipedia 'Czechoslovak arms deal (1955)', 'Aswan Dam'; Devlin, Chief of Station, Congo (2007); Church Committee Interim Report 'Alleged Assassination Plots' (Nov 1975).

findings.title: Non-alignment was an active third attractor with its own goods — prestige, conference hosting, double-sourced aid, base refusals, and UN votes — and its own cost: no security guarantee
findings.detail: The goods were concrete. Prestige and hosting: Bandung (18-24 Apr 1955, 29 states), Belgrade (1-6 Sept 1961, 25 states), Cairo (Oct 1964, 47 states), Accra's All-African Peoples' Conference (Dec 1958). Double sourcing: India took Bhilai from the USSR (1955), Rourkela from West Germany, Durgapur from Britain; Egypt took Aswan from Moscow and PL-480 wheat from Washington until 1965. Base refusal as a status good: Morocco negotiated the US SAC bases out (agreed Dec 1959, gone 1963); Ceylon closed Trincomalee and Katunayake to Britain (1957); Nkrumah and Toure refused any base; Libya, the counter-example, leased Wheelus to the USAF until 1970 and was the poorest and most 'available' of them. UN votes: the Afro-Asian caucus authored Res 1514 (14 Dec 1960, 89-0-9). The cost: non-alignment bought no protection — India had to take US/UK emergency arms in Oct-Nov 1962 and then Soviet MiG-21 licences; Sukarno's 'Nefos' posture ended in the Sept 1965 massacre. The bloc also had internal camps (Casablanca group Jan 1961: Ghana, Guinea, Mali, Egypt, Morocco vs Monrovia/Brazzaville group), and from 1963 a fourth attractor appeared: China (Zhou Enlai's Africa tour Dec 1963-Feb 1964, TAZARA agreed 1967). For the game this settles the sketch's open question: Non-Aligned must be an attractor whose pull scales with the number and prestige of states already in it, whose members are harder to move than bloc members because their legitimacy is invested in it, and whose payout is UN weight rather than bases or trade.
findings.evidence: Prashad, The Darker Nations (2007); Westad 2005; Wikipedia 'Bandung Conference', '1st Summit of the Non-Aligned Movement', 'Casablanca Group', 'Wheelus Air Base', 'Sino-Indian War' aftermath; Mazov 2010 on China's entry; Zhou Enlai 'Africa is ripe for revolution' (Mogadishu, 3 Feb 1964).

findings.title: The 1963-66 coup wave had structural, legible causes: army size, discharged veterans, officer-training source, ethnic-regional composition, and party militias — a data-driven coup surface, not dice
findings.detail: Africa's first post-independence coup, Togo 13 Jan 1963: Sylvanus Olympio was killed by ex-French army NCOs (Eyadema among them) after refusing to expand a 250-man army to absorb ~600 veterans demobilized from Algeria and Indochina. Then Congo-Brazzaville (Aug 1963), Dahomey (Oct 1963), Gabon (Feb 1964, reversed by France), Algeria (19 June 1965, Boumediene over Ben Bella), Congo-Leopoldville (Mobutu, 24 Nov 1965), Dahomey again (Dec 1965), then in eight weeks: CAR (1 Jan 1966), Upper Volta (3 Jan), Nigeria (15 Jan, the majors; counter-coup 29 July; Biafra 30 May 1967), Ghana (24 Feb 1966, while Nkrumah flew to Hanoi via Peking). The mechanism in each case is readable from three variables: (1) whether the government's power base was the army or a party, (2) whether the army's lean diverged from the government's — Nkrumah's Soviet-trained President's Own Guard Regiment versus a British-trained officer corps; Nigeria's Igbo-heavy officer corps versus a Northern-led government; Algeria's external ALN under Boumediene versus Ben Bella's civilian FLN, and (3) stability. The survivors show the counter-moves: Toure purged the army and armed a party militia (the 'permanent plot'), Nyerere disbanded the Tanganyika Rifles and rebuilt a TANU-affiliated force. Twilight Struggle already encodes the threshold well (coup succeeds if ops + die > 2 x stability), and UGS already has a dynamic per-country stability; what is missing is the army-vs-government lean divergence that makes some states coup-prone at equal stability.
findings.evidence: Decalo, Coups and Army Rule in Africa (1976); Luckham, The Nigerian Military (1971); First, The Barrel of a Gun (1970); Huntington, Political Order in Changing Societies (1968); Stockwell, In Search of Enemies (1978) on the Ghana station; Wikipedia '1963 Togolese coup d'etat', '1966 Nigerian coup d'etat', '1966 Ghanaian coup d'etat', 'Tanganyika Rifles mutiny'; GMT Twilight Struggle rulebook 6.3.5 (coup formula).

findings.title: The UN General Assembly was the actual Cold War scoreboard, and 1960 is the year the West lost the automatic majority — which is exactly when non-alignment started to matter
findings.detail: Membership: 51 (1945), 60 (1950), 76 after the 14 Dec 1955 package deal, 99 after 20 Sept 1960 (17 admitted in one day: 16 African states plus Cyprus), 117 by 1965. The US built UNGA into a weapon while it held the majority (Uniting for Peace, Res 377, 3 Nov 1950; the Korea votes) and then lost it: Res 1514 (Declaration on Granting Independence, 14 Dec 1960) passed 89-0-9 with the US abstaining alongside Britain, France, Belgium, Portugal, Spain, South Africa; Res 1761 on South Africa sanctions (6 Nov 1962) passed 67-16-23 over Western objections; Chinese representation had to be converted into an 'important question' needing two-thirds (Res 1668, 15 Dec 1961) to hold, and fell anyway in Res 2758 (25 Oct 1971, 76-35-17, with 26 African votes for Peking). Khrushchev went to the 15th session personally (Sept-Oct 1960, the shoe on 12 Oct) because the seventeen new votes were in the room; Nkrumah, Toure, Nasser, Tito, Sukarno and Castro all spoke that session. The vote is the payout mechanism the influence pillar lacks: it is periodic (Sept-Dec sessions), tabulated, public, and differs by issue (a Commonwealth state votes with London on Rhodesia but with the Afro-Asians on decolonization), so it turns alignment plus non-alignment plus metropole loyalty into one comparable number per year that era-checkpoint victory can read.
findings.evidence: UN 'Growth in United Nations membership' (un.org); UNGA Res 377 (1950), 1514 (XV) and 1541 (XV) (14-15 Dec 1960), 1668 (XVI), 1761 (XVII), 2758 (XXVI) with roll-call tallies in the UN Yearbook; Wikipedia 'Shoe-banging incident', 'Year of Africa'.

findings.title: Game precedents converge: contests need a close date and a scoring surface, adjacency matters, alignment and regime type must be orthogonal, and 'nobody won' must not be the neutral state
findings.detail: Twilight Struggle (GMT, 2005; Deluxe 2009): regional scoring cards (Africa: presence 1 / domination 4 / control 6, battlegrounds Algeria, Angola, Nigeria, South Africa, Zaire) make regions score at unpredictable but bounded moments; 'Decolonization' (USSR, 2 ops: +1 in four Africa/SE Asia countries) and 'Colonial Rear Guards' (US) are literally opening bids; realignment rolls add +1 per adjacent controlled country, so a foothold in Ghana reaches Togo. Its weakness is instructive: non-aligned = zero influence = nothing, so the third attractor does not exist. Labyrinth (GMT, 2010) separates governance (Good/Fair/Poor/Islamist) from alignment (Ally/Neutral/Adversary) and scores both — the orthogonal-axes model UGS needs for regime type vs bloc. Victoria 3 (Paradox, 2022; Sphere of Influence DLC, June 2024, 1.7): interest groups (armed forces, intelligentsia, trade unions, landowners, devout) with clout in or out of government are the per-faction alignment structure the sketch asks about, and Power Blocs add sway actions, lobbies and cohesion — its failure mode is that sway is a click-per-country grind. Terra Invicta (Pavonis, 2022): control points per nation gated by public-opinion campaigns, with legible prerequisites and rival purges, is the best model for 'you can see why your bid is losing'. HoI4 Together for Victory (Dec 2016) autonomy ladder (Integrated Puppet -> Puppet -> Dominion -> Free) with drift from lend-lease and trade is the commitment-depth ladder, criticized mainly for being invisible until threshold. Balance of Power (Crawford, 1985; 1990 edition) had the right verb set (economic aid, military aid, insurgency aid, destabilization, treaty, diplomatic pressure, intervention) scored by prestige, and showed that unattributed passive drift feels arbitrary.
findings.evidence: GMT Twilight Struggle rulebook and card list (Deluxe ed. 2009); GMT Labyrinth: The War on Terror rulebook (2010) sec. 5; Paradox Victoria 3 dev diaries #92-#95 (Sphere of Influence, 2024) and wiki 'Interest groups'; Terra Invicta wiki 'Control Point', 'Public Campaign'; Paradox HoI4 wiki 'Autonomy' (TfV); Crawford, Balance of Power: International Politics as the Ultimate Global Game (1986).

findings.title: Aid that moved alignment was a placed, named project — and the biggest ones were auctioned — so the opening should reuse the project machinery the economy pillar already built
findings.detail: The bids people remembered were objects on the map, not budget lines: Aswan (US/UK/World Bank offer Dec 1955, withdrawn 19 July 1956, Soviet finance agreed Dec 1958), Bhilai steel (1955), Volta/Akosombo (agreements 1961-62, VALCO smelter with Ex-Im backing), Conakry's Soviet stadium, printing presses and Il-18 airline, Mali's Soviet cement works, Afghanistan's Salang tunnel (1964), TAZARA (1967-75, China's largest foreign project). Arms were placed too: the Czech arms deal of Sept 1955 delivered ~200 MiG-15s and tanks and reset Egypt's officer corps' orientation. The economic-agency research already defers 'contested foreign bids / the Aswan auction (reuses project machinery, fuses pillars 2-4)'; the independence opening is the natural first consumer: an aid bid is a project placed on the newborn state's region, drawn from the bidder's construction pool, with completion as a step-change the recipient's economy feels and the newspaper prints. That prices aid in the currency the player already manages (pool capacity and material gating), keeps decision counts capped by the project slot budget, and makes rival bids visible on the map through espionage fidelity.
findings.evidence: docs/research/economic-agency.md (deferred: 'Contested foreign bids / the Aswan auction'); Wikipedia 'Aswan Dam' (financing chronology), 'Akosombo Dam', 'Bhilai Steel Plant', 'TAZARA Railway', 'Czechoslovak arms deal (1955)'; Goldman 1967; Mazov 2010 on Guinea project list.

findings.title: Cadre formation was the slow verb with the longest lag: scholarships, officer training, and volunteers set the lean of the NEXT government
findings.detail: Both sides bought the second generation. Moscow founded Peoples' Friendship University on 5 Feb 1960 (renamed for Lumumba 22 Feb 1961) and trained Ghanaian, Guinean, Malian and Algerian officers and pilots; Washington answered with the Kenya student airlift (Tom Mboya, 81 students 11 Sept 1959; the Kennedy Foundation's $100,000 in Aug 1960 after State refused, ~800 students by 1963, Barack Obama Sr. among them), the Peace Corps (created 1 Mar 1961; the first 51 volunteers landed in Ghana 30 Aug 1961), and Sandhurst/Fort Leavenworth slots for officers. France kept the largest cadre pipeline of all through the technical assistants and the ecole militaire slots that produced Eyadema and Bokassa. The payoff lagged five to ten years and landed on the faction the trainee joined — which is exactly why the army lean (training source) and party lean (scholarship source) should be separate attributes: Soviet-trained officers were the Ghana army's minority and the coup came from the British-trained majority; the Guinea 'teachers' plot' was a party-cadre fight. A cadre bid is therefore cheap, invisible to the current government, and its output is a modifier on the next transition (coup, election, succession), not on today's alignment.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia 'Peoples' Friendship University of Russia', 'Airlift Africa' / Shachtman, Airlift to America (2009); Peace Corps history (peacecorps.gov, Ghana I); Mazov 2010 on Soviet military training; Decalo 1976 on French-trained NCOs.

findings.title: Engine collision: the existing chain events already hard-set newborn alignments, and 37 CountryDefs carry scripted alignments — the opening must own those outcomes or be overwritten by them
findings.detail: Today ghana-pan-african-course (EventFired ghana-independence +642 days, a GHA-only decision) and guinea-courts-moscow (+300 days) resolve alignment via SetAlignment, katanga-reintegrated hard-sets COD to WesternBloc, and every state in countries/independence.ron ships with a baseline Alignment that Military::alignment_of returns until overridden. A contest system that resolves alignment would be overwritten by these scripts (or vice versa) depending on tick order. The clean move is to keep the events as content but retarget them: the leader-decision events become bids or lean deltas into the open contest (Nkrumah's Accra conference = a Non-Aligned pole bonus; Moscow's lifeline = an Eastern bid the AI makes on schedule), and the Independence effect itself opens the contest rather than SetAlignment closing it. The existing per-province Independence with majority-rule region ownership and the occupation overlay's popular alignment (from war-termination) are already the substrate for a 'street' lean per region — Katanga is a region whose street disagrees with Leopoldville.
findings.evidence: crates/ugs-sim/src/events.rs lines ~210-290 (SetAlignment insert, Independence effect); assets/data/scenario/1950/events/07-sub-saharan-africa-1950-.ron ('ghana-pan-african-course', 'guinea-courts-moscow', 'katanga-reintegrated'); assets/data/scenario/1950/countries/independence.ron (37 defs with baseline alignment); docs/design/systems/world-timeline.md 'Dynamic world state' rule that all reads go through alignment_of.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: The Independence Opening: a time-boxed contest object opened by every Independence effect (and, later, by any regime transition)
mechanics_recommendations.why: History shows a real, short, observable bidding window (Vietnam recognition Jan-Feb 1950; Guinea Oct 1958-1959; Congo's eleven weeks in 1960) that closed on regime consolidation. A window with a printed close date is what Twilight Struggle's scoring cards and Imperial Struggle's investment turns get right: pressure to commit now, and a moment of resolution the newspaper can report. It converts the scripted timeline into 'scripted timing, unscripted outcomes' as the vision doc demands.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Open at the Independence event (optionally a pre-opening 6-12 months earlier for dated cases like Libya, whose UN date was fixed by Res 289 on 21 Nov 1949) and close at a data-driven horizon (default 12 months; Congo-type collapses close early on a coup). Bidders: Western pole, Eastern pole, the former metropole (a separate AI with its own residual weight: France high, Britain medium, Belgium withdrawn), and the Non-Aligned pole whose weight is derived, not bid — number of non-aligned states, prestige of hosts (Bandung 1955, Belgrade 1961), and the newborn leader's power base. The player reads one OPENING dossier per contest: a verdict sentence ('CONGO: OPEN. GOVERNMENT BASE: PARTY (WEAK). ARMY: BELGIAN-OFFICERED. CLOSES 30 JUN 1961 OR ON COLLAPSE.'), a bid table of what each side has committed as you believe it (rival bids rendered through espionage fidelity), and verb buttons. Decision it changes: which two or three openings to spend this year's aid slots and arms on, versus posture-only recognition for the rest.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Bids as five typed verbs with distinct signatures: recognition, aid project, arms and officer training, cadres, and base request — plus covert as the sixth through the espionage system
mechanics_recommendations.why: The sketch lists aid, diplomacy, propaganda, election interference and coup sponsorship but does not say how they differ; the record says they differ by speed, visibility, which faction they move, and what they cost the bidder. Recognition is instant, cheap, visible, and mostly signals (US vs USSR on Vietnam, Feb 1950). Aid projects are slow and public and move the government (Volta, Bhilai). Arms and training are medium-speed and move the army's lean (Czech arms 1955; Ghana's POGR). Cadres are cheap, invisible, and move the next government (Lumumba University, the Kenya airlift, Peace Corps). A base request buys commitment depth for the bidder but pushes the state toward Non-Aligned prestige if refused (Morocco, Ceylon), and Libya-style acceptance costs the host legitimacy.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Each verb writes to a different lean: government lean (recognition, aid, diplomacy), army lean (arms, training source), party/cadre lean (scholarships, volunteers), street lean per region (propaganda, visible projects, reuse of the occupation overlay's popular alignment). Aid bids are literal projects placed on the newborn's region from the bidder's construction pool (the deferred 'Aswan auction' machinery), with completion as a step change; arms bids are GrantStock with a training-source tag; cadre bids are a standing flow with a 5-10 year payout. Costs are paid in currencies that already exist: pool capacity, stock, tension (an arms bid into a contested opening adds tenths; Congo 1960 did), and legitimacy for the metropole. Covert bids (a pre-independence network, a purchased officer) route through intel.rs and its exposure clock. Player reads: the bid table with an estimate-language forecast ('EAST LEADS: PROBABLE') derived only from visible factors, never a percentage. Decision it changes: which faction you are buying, knowing that buying the army in a party-state (Ghana) is buying a future coup, not today's alignment.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Resolution writes four things, and Non-Aligned outcomes are stickier: alignment (the existing three-valued enum), a hidden lean (-100..100), commitment depth (sympathetic / aligned / treaty / satellite), and regime type plus power base
mechanics_recommendations.why: Labyrinth's governance-vs-alignment split and HoI4's autonomy ladder show that a bloc tag alone is illegible and unsticky. The historical record shows non-aligned states were harder to move (India never moved; Ghana and Guinea cost both blocs a decade of aid for votes) because non-alignment was the regime's legitimacy, while metropole-committed states (Ivory Coast) never even entered the market, and no-base states (Congo) flipped on a coup. Commitment depth is what makes satellites and clients (already objects in war-termination) continuous with sympathetic states.
mechanics_recommendations.how: At close, sum bids weighted by the leader's power base and the metropole's residual: party-state leaders discount aid and weight cadres and prestige; metropole-groomed leaders weight the metropole's defense agreement; army-based regimes weight arms. Output alignment is the leading pole if its margin exceeds a threshold, else NonAligned. Commitment depth starts at sympathetic and rises to treaty only via an explicit treaty/base bid the recipient accepted. Inertia is a per-country number: NonAligned resolutions get the highest inertia (moving them later costs 2x and requires a transition event), treaty states the next, sympathetic the least — so 'we lost the opening to non-alignment' is worse than 'we lost it to the other side by a hair' in a way the player can read. Regime type and power base are written from the resolution (party-state if the winning bids were cadres/prestige, military if arms dominated, metropole-parliamentary if the metropole won) and become CountryDef-style runtime overrides behind the existing alignment_of accessor pattern. The player reads it as a one-line verdict in the newspaper ('GHANA GOES NON-ALIGNED; PARTY-STATE; HARD TO MOVE') and on the influence map mode as tint plus a depth hatch. Decision it changes: whether to keep spending on a closed state or wait for its next transition.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Faction leans as the coup and drift surface, with a legible clock instead of a die: army lean vs government lean divergence times low stability times a trigger, and the metropole's reversal right
mechanics_recommendations.why: The 1963-66 wave was structurally caused (veterans, training source, ethnic composition, party militias) and structurally prevented (Toure's purge, Nyerere's rebuild, France's Gabon paratroopers). The espionage research's house rules say risk must be a visible clock and outcomes a ladder, not a percentage; Twilight Struggle's coup-vs-2x-stability threshold is already legible and UGS has dynamic stability. Coup sponsorship as a verb then means 'raise the army's lean toward you and lower stability', which makes it distinct from election interference (moves street lean in parliamentary regimes) and from propaganda.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Each state carries government lean, army lean, party lean, and per-region street lean. A monthly 'praetorian pressure' value = |army - government| scaled by (100 - stability) plus discrete factors printed as lines (DISCHARGED VETERANS UNABSORBED; FOREIGN-TRAINED GUARD REGIMENT; OFFICER CORPS FROM ONE REGION). Above a threshold the state enters a COUP-PRONE band the player can see; a sponsored coup is an intel op whose outcome ladder is: clean transition (army lean becomes government lean, regime becomes military), messy transition (stability crash, street revolt in dissenting regions, Katanga-style secession using the existing occupation overlay), failure with purge (leader purges army, raises party militia, inertia up), and loud exposure (tension and world-opinion cost, attribution three-state machine). The metropole holds a reversal right while a defense agreement exists (Gabon 1964; Tanganyika 1964): a one-shot decision event offered to the metropole player/AI within 48 hours of a coup, costing legitimacy and stock. Recipients get counter-verbs: absorb veterans (stock cost), purge the army (stability cost, inertia gain), build a party militia. Player reads: the state's dossier verdict ('NIGERIA: COUP-PRONE. OFFICER CORPS EASTERN-REGIONAL; GOVERNMENT NORTHERN') and the wire when the band changes. Decision it changes: sponsor, shore up, or pre-empt by offering the metropole a reason to intervene.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: The UN General Assembly session as the annual scoring surface, printed as the newspaper's INFLUENCE STANDINGS page, and read by era-checkpoint victory
mechanics_recommendations.why: The UNGA was the actual scoreboard, and the 20 Sept 1960 admission of seventeen states flipped the majority — the moment non-alignment starts to pay. Without it, a Non-Aligned outcome has no payout for anyone and reverts to Twilight Struggle's 'nobody won'. A vote also makes alignment issue-specific (Commonwealth loyalty on Rhodesia, Afro-Asian solidarity on 1514), which is how a metropole's residual can be scored without inventing a fourth alignment value.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Each September a session opens with three to five resolutions from a data file (Uniting for Peace 1950, Korea 1951, Hungary 1956, Algeria 1957-60, Res 1514 Dec 1960, Chinese representation yearly as an important question from 1961, South Africa 1962, test ban 1963), each with issue tags (colonial, bloc, security). Every member's vote is computed from alignment, lean, metropole loyalty on colonial tags, and non-aligned solidarity, with a small deterministic vote-buying window: a 'seat sponsorship' or aid bid in the 90 days before the session can swing a NonAligned member's vote on one resolution. The roll call is published as a tally per pole and as the newspaper's INFLUENCE STANDINGS page (bloc counts, non-aligned count, votes swung), date-stamped and still, per the economy house rules. Era-checkpoint victory (1955, 1960, 1965) reads the last session's tallies and membership share. The player reads standings monthly and the vote annually; the decision it changes is whether to spend an aid slot on a swing member in August or on an opening in Africa.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Wave handling for 1960: regional openings, a slot cap, and a default posture so decision count stays a designed budget
mechanics_recommendations.why: The engine fires seventeen independences in 1960 and the economy house rules cap player decisions at roughly two to four per month; seventeen dossiers is Victoria 3 whack-a-mole. Historically the wave was also handled regionally: the French Community bloc negotiated as one, the Brazzaville group voted as one, Nixon's 1957 Ghana trip and Khrushchev's 1960 UN visit were single moves aimed at a set.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Independence events tagged with a wave id (french-west-africa-1960, equatorial-1960, east-africa-1963) open one regional opening with per-state sub-rows; a bid can be placed on the region (spread thin, metropole-style) or on one state (Guinea-style concentration), mirroring Moscow's historically concentrated credits. The player has N concurrent active bids (three in v1, one Great-Project-scale), everything else runs a standing posture chosen once per pole: recognize-and-embassy (free, sympathetic-only outcomes) or ignore (cedes to metropole and Non-Aligned). The AI poles and metropoles bid by the same rules with the historical concentrations as data (France everywhere in its Community, USSR on Guinea/Ghana/Mali, US on Congo/Nigeria). Reads as a single WAVE dossier with a ranked row per state (a triage list, not a data lake). Decision it changes: which two states in the wave get real bids, and whether to fight the metropole for its own bloc's states or let it hold them.

pitfalls: Fungible influence points (Twilight Struggle's bank-account model) applied to 226 countries: alignment becomes a number you top up, every state plays the same, and the leader/army/party texture that actually decided outcomes disappears. Keep the leans typed and the bids typed; never expose a raw 'influence' total to the player.

Non-Aligned as the residual 'nobody won' state. If it has no goods (UN weight, prestige, hosting) and no inertia, every AI bidder will eventually push every state into a bloc and the Bandung world never appears. It must be an attractor with a derived pull and the highest inertia, and the UN vote must pay it out.

The 1960 wave breaks the decision budget. Seventeen simultaneous OPENING dossiers each demanding bids is exactly the whack-a-mole the economy research warns about; without regional bundling, slot caps, and a default posture the pillar ships as a chore.

Silent collisions with the shipped timeline: chain events (ghana-pan-african-course, guinea-courts-moscow, katanga-reintegrated) and the 37 baseline CountryDefs hard-set alignment. If the contest and the scripts both write alignments, the last writer in tick order wins and the player sees a flip they never caused. Retarget those events into bids or lean deltas before shipping the contest.

Coups as percentage rolls. The espionage house rules (visible clock, outcome ladder, failure is content) apply to coup sponsorship exactly; a coup that succeeds on a hidden roll reads as a betrayal and one that fails silently reads as nothing happened.

Pricing aid in money the superpower player does not feel. A newborn state's whole economy is a rounding error to the US or USSR pool; if bids cost money, every opening gets bought by whoever clicks first. Price bids in slots, pool capacity, materials, tension, and legitimacy, which are already scarce.

Modeling the metropole as merely a Western-bloc appendage. France in Guinea, Portugal in Angola, and Britain at Suez all diverged from Washington; if the metropole cannot lose a state to its own bloc's patron, the US-courting-what-France-is-losing dynamic (and the abstentions on Res 1514) cannot occur, and playing France or Britain has no pillar-2 game.

Leaders as full sim objects. The timeline doc deliberately deferred leaders; the opening only needs regime type and power base enums with runtime overrides. Building a leader system first delays the whole pillar and duplicates the timeline's death-and-succession events.
analysts.first_hour_test: Playing the US or USSR from 1 Jan 1950, the top bar's new OPENINGS indicator shows three live contests before the first month ends, none of them invented: (1) VIETNAM — a recognition race with a days-long close: Peking recognizes the DRV on 18 Jan, Moscow on 30 Jan, and the player is offered recognition of Bao Dai's State of Vietnam (historically 7 Feb); the dossier's verdict reads 'ASSOCIATED STATES: METROPOLE (FRANCE) HOLDS; STREET LEANS EAST IN TONKIN; CLOSES ON RECOGNITION'; a one-click verb, and the newspaper's February issue prints who recognized whom. (2) INDONESIA — independent since 27 Dec 1949, still inside its twelve-month window, closing on UN admission (28 Sept 1950): the player can place one aid bid (the historical $100m Ex-Im loan of Feb 1950 is the Western AI's default bid if the player does not act) and reads a believed bid table where the Soviet column shows 'UNKNOWN' until the embassy network reports. (3) LIBYA — a pre-opening with a printed close of 24 Dec 1951 (UN Res 289 of Nov 1949) where a base request (Wheelus) is on the table and the verdict warns that pressing it pushes the outcome toward Non-Aligned prestige. By June 1950, before the 25 June invasion, the player has made two or three pillar-2 decisions, one opening has resolved with a verdict headline, the June newspaper's INFLUENCE STANDINGS page shows the membership tally that the Uniting for Peace vote in November will draw on, and one state's dossier now says 'SYMPATHETIC (WEST); HARD TO MOVE: NO'. That proves the loop — see an opening, choose a typed bid, watch it resolve, read the standing — is playable inside the tutorial peace, with Ghana 1957 and the 1960 wave as the same loop at scale.

findings.title: Western allies never defected; they hedged through the electoral valve while a quarter of the electorate voted for the other side
findings.detail: In France the PCF polled 28.3% (Nov 1946), 26.9% (June 1951, still the largest party by votes, cut to 103 seats by the apparentements law) and 25.9% (Jan 1956, 150 seats); it was expelled from government in May 1947 and never returned, so for a decade the GOVERNMENT of France was Western while the STREET was a third hostile. Italy: DC 48.5% vs Popular Front 31.0% in April 1948, then PCI 22.6% (1953), 22.7% (1958), 25.3% (1963), 26.9% (1968), rising every election under the conventio ad excludendum. The patron's tools were money and conditionality, not force: Marshall's March 1948 statement that aid would stop under a communist government, the Letters-to-Italy campaign, and covert party funding the Pike Committee (1976) put at roughly $65-75M for Italy 1948-68. The lesson for the model: an ally's alignment can be safe at the government level and contested at the street level for twenty years, and the only channel through which the street reaches the government in a democracy is a scheduled election. Elections are therefore a VALVE with a date, not a random event: the player's verbs happen before the date (credits, conditional aid, covert party funding) and the outcome is read on the date. One scalar per country cannot express 'safe government, hostile street'; it collapses France 1951 into either 'Western' or 'contested', and both are wrong.
findings.evidence: French legislative elections 17 June 1951 and 2 Jan 1956 (Ministry of the Interior results); Italian general elections 18 Apr 1948, 7 Jun 1953, 25 May 1958, 28 Apr 1963, 19 May 1968; George Marshall statement of 20 Mar 1948; Pike Committee report (leaked to The Village Voice, Feb 1976); Kaeten Mistry, The United States, Italy and the Origins of Cold War (2014); Paul Ginsborg, A History of Contemporary Italy (1990); the EDC vote of 30 Aug 1954 (319-264, Gaullists plus Communists) as the case of an ally's domestic politics killing a bloc project outright.

findings.title: Western drift is a change of commitment depth, not of alignment: de Gaulle, Iceland 1956, Anpo 1960, Godesberg 1959
findings.detail: Every Western 'threat to alignment' the brief lists ended with the country still in the Western bloc but at a different depth. De Gaulle: Sept 1958 memorandum demanding a tripartite directorate, Mediterranean fleet withdrawn from NATO command March 1959, letter to Johnson 7 March 1966 leaving the integrated command, SHAPE moved to Casteau by March 1967, 26,000 US troops gone by April 1967, and the North Atlantic Treaty itself untouched. Iceland: the Althing voted 28 March 1956 to have US forces leave Keflavik; after Hungary and Suez the same leftist coalition signed the 6 Dec 1956 agreement keeping them, sweetened with American loans. Japan: Kishi rammed treaty ratification through on 19-20 May 1960 with police carrying Socialist deputies out of the chamber, Michiko Kanba died 15 June, Eisenhower's visit was cancelled 16 June, Kishi resigned (formally 15 July), Ikeda pivoted to the Income Doubling Plan of 27 Dec 1960 and the treaty stood. West Germany: the SPD opposed rearmament, the EDC, NATO accession (1955) and nuclear arming (Kampf dem Atomtod, 1958), then accepted the market at Bad Godesberg 13-15 Nov 1959 and Western integration in Wehner's Bundestag speech of 30 June 1960; Adenauer's 1957 absolute majority (50.2%) was won on 'Keine Experimente'. Britain: the Bevanite resignations of April 1951, Labour's Scarborough conference voting unilateral disarmament 5 Oct 1960 and reversing it at Blackpool 1961, Wilson refusing Johnson troops for Vietnam in 1964-65 while staying East of Suez. The sketch's depth ladder (sympathetic, aligned, treaty member, satellite) is exactly the axis these cases move on, and the current three-valued `Alignment` enum cannot represent any of them: the shipped `france-nato-exit` event has to price it as legitimacy and stability because there is nothing else to move. Depth must be a first-class per-country field the victory checkpoints score, and Western 'drift' should almost always be a one-rung depth loss with basing and command consequences, never a bloc flip.
findings.evidence: Frederic Bozo, Two Strategies for Europe: De Gaulle, the United States and the Atlantic Alliance (2001); Valur Ingimundarson, 'Buttressing the West in the North: The Atlantic Alliance, Economic Warfare, and the Soviet Challenge in Iceland, 1956-1959', International History Review 21:1 (1999); Nick Kapur, Japan at the Crossroads: Conflict and Compromise after Anpo (2018); SPD Godesberger Programm, 15 Nov 1959; Labour Party Conference Report 1960; the game's own assets/data/scenario/1950/events/03-western-europe.ron `france-nato-exit` (priced without a depth field).

findings.title: The market patron disciplines through credit and arms, and the cost is paid in the ally's street; it sometimes topples governments and sometimes drives the ally toward a hedging pole
findings.detail: The West's equivalent of tanks was the ledger. Suez: Eisenhower refused IMF support for sterling until the 6 Nov 1956 ceasefire, and Eden fell in January 1957. Canada: the State Department press release of 30 Jan 1963 contradicting Diefenbaker on Bomarc warheads brought his government down on 5 Feb 1963 and Pearson won on 8 April. Turkey: the Johnson letter of 5 June 1964 forbidding a Cyprus landing turned Turkish public opinion against Washington and opened the 1965-67 Soviet economic overtures; the 1960 coup (27 May; Menderes hanged 17 Sept 1961) had not touched NATO membership at all. Pakistan: the 1965 US arms embargo pushed Ayub toward Beijing. Greece: the colonels' coup of 21 April 1967 was tolerated, at a legitimacy price to Washington in every European capital, because the alternative was an election the left front might contest (EDA had polled 24.4% and become official opposition in 1958). Australia is the inverse: the Petrov defection of 3 April 1954 helped Menzies win the 29 May 1954 election and split Labor in 1955. The mechanic this dictates: a market patron's discipline verbs are conditional credits, arms supply, and public pressure, they act through the client's domestic seats (moving the street against the patron even when they get the government they wanted), and they are the pillar-4 mirror of the planned patron's garrison. The asymmetry lives in the discipline verb, exactly as the economy research said it should live in the decision stream.
findings.evidence: Diane Kunz, The Economic Diplomacy of the Suez Crisis (1991); Jocelyn Ghent, 'Did He Fall or Was He Pushed? The Kennedy Administration and the Collapse of the Diefenbaker Government', International History Review 1:2 (1979); the Johnson letter to Inonu, 5 June 1964 (FRUS 1964-68 vol. XVI); Greek general election of 11 May 1958 results; Robert Manne, The Petrov Affair (1987).

findings.title: Eastern satellites drift when the patron's own line shifts or its garrison leaves; the trigger is always in the patron's decision log, so the player can be shown it coming
findings.detail: Berlin 17 June 1953 was triggered by the 28 May 1953 work-norm increase colliding with the post-Stalin New Course of 9-11 June that relaxed everything except the norms; roughly 500,000 people in some 700 localities, at least 55 dead, Ulbricht strengthened and Beria arrested nine days later. Poznan 28 June 1956 and the Polish October were the Secret Speech (25 Feb 1956) arriving in a bloc whose parties had been built on Stalin; Khrushchev flew uninvited to Warsaw on 19 Oct 1956 with Soviet columns moving and backed down when Polish internal-security troops deployed. Hungary was the same shock plus a leadership Moscow had itself destabilized (Rakosi removed July 1956). Albania: Khrushchev's pilgrimage to Tito (Belgrade Declaration, 2 June 1955) terrified Hoxha, who feared Yugoslav absorption, and the break of 3 Dec 1961 followed the Vlore submarine quarrel and the cutting of Soviet credits, with Chinese ones arriving. China: the cancelled sample-bomb agreement (20 June 1959), Camp David (Sept 1959), and the withdrawal of 1,390 advisers in July-Aug 1960. Romania: Soviet troops left in summer 1958, which is what made the April 1964 Declaration against Comecon's Valev plan survivable; there was no garrison to send. In every case the satellite's drift began with a patron decision (de-Stalinize, reconcile with a satellite's enemy, withdraw the garrison, cancel a credit). Drift should therefore be computed from the patron's own recorded choices (the `OptionChosen` stamps already exist) plus garrison presence, and the embassy report can name the cause: 'RESENTMENT IN TIRANA RISING SINCE THE BELGRADE DECLARATION'. That makes the mirror legible and makes it the player's fault, which is the point.
findings.evidence: Christian Ostermann (ed.), Uprising in East Germany 1953 (CWIHP, 2001); Hope Harrison, Driving the Soviets up the Wall (2003); Mark Kramer, 'The Malin Notes on the Crises in Hungary and Poland, 1956', CWIHP Bulletin 8-9 (1996-97); Elidor Mehilli, From Stalin to Mao: Albania and the Socialist World (2017); Lorenz Luthi, The Sino-Soviet Split (2008); Dennis Deletant, Romania under Communist Rule (1999); Soviet withdrawal from Romania, June-July 1958.

findings.title: There are two crushes, purge and invasion, with very different bills; the invasion's bill is paid mostly in the rival bloc's domestic seats and in delayed memory, not in lasting state-level tension
findings.detail: The cheap crush is pre-emptive: after Tito's expulsion (Cominform resolution, 28 June 1948) Stalin purged every other party rather than invade Yugoslavia: Rajk (tried 16-24 Sept 1949), Kostov (Dec 1949), Gomulka (removed Nov 1949, arrested Aug 1951, with Rokossovsky installed as Polish defence minister 7 Nov 1949), Slansky (Nov 1952). Purges cost the satellite stability and the party its cadres, and nothing in tension or world opinion; nobody outside cared. The expensive crush is Operation Whirlwind: ~2,500-3,000 Hungarians and ~700 Soviet soldiers dead, 200,000 refugees, Nagy hanged 16 June 1958. Its real bill: the CPGB lost roughly a quarter of its members (about 33,000 in Feb 1956 to about 25,000 by Feb 1958, with E.P. Thompson's The Reasoner group walking out), the CPUSA collapsed toward 3,000 by 1958, the PCI shed members and most of its intellectuals (the 'manifesto of the 101'), Sartre broke with the PCF; Iceland's leftist government reversed its base vote within six weeks. Meanwhile the state-level cost was small and short: Eisenhower called Hungary 'as inaccessible as Tibet', the simultaneous Suez war (29 Oct-7 Nov) halved the propaganda payoff, and the 'liberation' rhetoric of Radio Free Europe was exposed as bluff, a legitimacy cost to the West. Prague 1968 repeats the pattern: five-army invasion 20-21 Aug 1968, condemnation by the PCI and PCF and the birth of Eurocommunism, Ceausescu's balcony speech, Albania leaving the Warsaw Pact in September, and SALT talks opening in November 1969 regardless. And toleration is not free: Poland got Soviet credits and debt cancellation in Nov 1956 and then $95M in US credits in 1957, i.e. a tolerated satellite becomes a country the rival can aid; the corpus already models the precedent cost as stability contagion. So the crush bill goes to (1) the rival's domestic street seats moving away from you, (2) your own legitimacy, (3) garrison divisions and a hostile occupation-zone-like state, (4) a delayed memory that makes the next rising worse (1956 to 1968 to 1980), and (5) a short tension spike that decays as the meter already does. The tolerate bill goes to (1) credits or industry, (2) a bloc precedent, and (3) the rival gaining an aid verb there.
findings.evidence: Charles Gati, Failed Illusions: Moscow, Washington, Budapest and the 1956 Hungarian Revolt (2006); Johanna Granville, The First Domino (2004); John Callaghan, Cold War, Crisis and Conflict: The CPGB 1951-68 (2003) for membership figures; Tony Judt, Postwar (2005) ch. 9 on Western CPs after 1956; Kovalev's Pravda article of 26 Sept 1968 ('Sovereignty and the International Obligations of Socialist Countries'); the game's own `hungary-soviet-decision` event, which prices tolerate as -10 stability across five satellites (the precedent cost) and crush as +50 tension, -15 legitimacy and four spawned divisions but currently charges nothing in the rival bloc's domestic politics.

findings.title: Non-Aligned was not the Eastern bloc's only exit; after 1960 the second pole for a drifting satellite was Beijing
findings.detail: Albania went to China, not to Belgrade or Delhi; Romania triangulated between Moscow and Beijing (abstaining in the 1963 polemics, mediating in 1964); North Korea and North Vietnam balanced the two; Western communist parties split into Maoist splinters after the Open Letter of 14 July 1963; and the 1958 Taiwan Strait crisis showed Beijing could pull the whole bloc's tension without Moscow's consent. Tito's Yugoslavia, by contrast, took Western wheat from late 1950, MDAP military aid from Nov 1951, and joined NATO members Greece and Turkey in the Balkan Pact (Ankara 28 Feb 1953, Bled 9 Aug 1954) while remaining socialist: Non-Aligned as a destination that Washington could pay for. For the mirror this means drift needs a destination pole and the pole is context-dependent: for an Eastern satellite before 1960 the only exit is Tito's road (Non-Aligned, Western-subsidized); after the split the exit is often Chinese-subsidized orthodoxy. The current data already flips Albania to NonAligned, which is wrong in spirit: Hoxha was more Stalinist than Moscow. The v1 slice can keep three poles in the enum but should let an Eastern-bloc government seat carry a 'Peking line' flag from the `open-split-1961` chain so that drift, aid sources and world-opinion payouts route to the right rival.
findings.evidence: Sergey Radchenko, Two Suns in the Heavens: The Sino-Soviet Struggle for Supremacy 1962-1967 (2009); Luthi (2008); Mehilli (2017); Lorraine Lees, Keeping Tito Afloat: The United States, Yugoslavia and the Cold War (1997); the game's `albania-split` event (SetAlignment NonAligned) and `open-split-1961` chain in 01-east-asia-1950-1970.ron.

findings.title: Games with a single subject-loyalty scalar cannot distinguish elections, coups and uprisings; games with full interest groups can, at whack-a-mole cost; the workable middle is a fixed small category set with global rules
findings.detail: HoI4 autonomy (Together for Victory, 15 Dec 2016) is a 0-100 number the overlord farms with lend-lease and the subject AI never uses to break away; its party-popularity bars plus 'boost ideology' advisors and the coup decision are the canonical pay-to-flip exploit, and its democracy elections are cosmetic events. EU4 liberty desire (1.8 Art of War, Oct 2014) is a scalar but has the one thing worth stealing: the rival's 'Support Independence' verb, an external actor buying a subject's drift. Stellaris Overlord (3.4, 12 May 2022) adds holdings and negotiable agreement terms as overlord levers, still on one loyalty axis. Victoria 3 (Oct 2022) gives every country eight interest groups with clout and approval, so an Armed Forces IG with low approval is a coup and Trade Unions are an uprising: the verbs are distinct because the seats are distinct, and the cost is that 100 countries of IG management is the complaint that dominates its forums. Democracy 4 shows fixed named voter groups make elections legible but reduces to slider optimization. Suzerain (Torpor Games, 4 Dec 2020) and Crisis in the Kremlin (1991; Kremlingames remake Feb 2017) plus Ostalgie: The Berlin Wall (2018) make domestic politics vivid with three or four named blocs (Old Guard, reformers, army; hardliners, reformers, republics) and one recurring decision, 'reform, repress, or ask Moscow to intervene'. Twilight Struggle (GMT, 2005) proves a per-country influence scalar with a control threshold is enough for a two-player abstraction, but it has to express every domestic event as a card ('De Gaulle Leads France', 'Socialist Governments', 'Independent Reds') because it has no seats. The direct precedents for a small fixed category set in a Cold War map game are Chris Crawford's Balance of Power (1985; 1990 Edition) with per-country government, insurgents and each superpower's influence and the verbs economic aid, military aid, insurgent aid, intervene for government, intervene for insurgents, destabilize, diplomatic pressure, treaty; and 1989: Dawn of Freedom (GMT, 2012), which gives every Eastern-bloc country spaces of seven fixed types (Elite, Bureaucratic, Intelligentsia, Worker, Farmer, Church, Student) and resolves power struggles by which types you hold. Neither needs per-country special rules; the categories are uniform and the drama comes from which one is contested where.
findings.evidence: HoI4 Together for Victory dev diaries (Nov-Dec 2016); Paradox forum thread 'Puppets never break free' (2019); EU4 patch 1.8 notes; Stellaris Overlord dev diary #245 (Mar 2022); Victoria 3 interest-group dev diary #6 (2021) and the 1.3-1.5 patch cycle's IG complaints; Chris Crawford, Balance of Power: International Politics as the Ultimate Global Game (Microsoft Press, 1986); 1989: Dawn of Freedom rulebook (Matthews and Torgerson, GMT 2012); Twilight Struggle card list (Gupta and Matthews, GMT 2005).

findings.title: Answer to the open question: three uniform seats per country (GOVERNMENT, STREET, GUNS) plus depth and a regime valve; the opposition is derived, not stored
findings.detail: Every historical case above moves exactly one seat: elections move GOVERNMENT from STREET on a date (France 1951, Turkey 14 May 1950, Japan 1960); coups move GOVERNMENT from GUNS when the army's lean diverges from the government and stability is low (Turkey 1960, Greece 1967, Egypt 1952, Iraq 1958); uprisings are STREET against GOVERNMENT in a regime with no valve (Berlin 1953, Poznan, Budapest, Prague); purges are GOVERNMENT acting on itself and GUNS (1949-52); patron crushes use GUNS, the patron's or the client's (Kadar needed Soviet armor because Hungarian units handed rifles to the crowd, which is the 'army unreliable' reading). Four seats (adding an opposition party) is one too many: in a democracy the opposition IS the sign of the street's lean relative to the government, so it can be printed as a label ('OPPOSITION: PCF, HOSTILE') without state; in a one-party state there is no opposition seat, only a street. Three seats times 226 countries is 678 small integers, sortable in a BTreeMap, digest-folded, with one uniform monthly drift rule and no per-country AI. The game already has two of the three scalars: `OccupationZone.alignment` (-1000..1000 popular disposition) is the STREET seat for occupied ground and should be promoted to a country-level field; `stability` is the cohesion term that decides whether divergence turns into an election result, a coup or a rising. `Military::alignment_of` stays the single accessor and becomes a threshold over the GOVERNMENT seat plus depth, so bloc basing, the allocator, red lines and map tinting need no change. Regime valve (`GovernmentType`, already reserved by war-termination's post-slice notes): Democracy (valve = scheduled election, a data field with the real first date and cycle), Party-state (no valve; pressure accumulates until a rising or a purge), Military/junta (valve = GUNS). Depth (sympathetic, aligned, treaty, satellite) gates which patron verbs exist: only satellite depth allows purge and garrison; treaty depth allows conditional credits and arms; aligned allows aid; sympathetic allows propaganda and party funding only.
findings.evidence: Mapping of the 20 cases cited in the findings above to seats; the existing `OccupationZone` struct in crates/ugs-sim/src/settlement.rs (alignment i16 -1000..1000, control, insurgency) as the ready-made crushed-satellite state; the `domestic_annexation_gate` deferral in docs/design/systems/war-termination.md reserving a GovernmentType axis; Vic3's eight IGs versus 1989's seven spaces versus Crisis in the Kremlin's three factions as the granularity range in shipped games.

findings.title: Seeing it coming was an intelligence product with a deadline, and world attention modulated the bill
findings.detail: Andropov's embassy cables from Budapest through October 1956 gave the Presidium exact readings of party split and army unreliability; the Presidium nonetheless adopted a tolerate declaration on 30 Oct 1956 and reversed it on 31 Oct after Suez began, Liu Shaoqi pressed for firmness, and reports arrived that Nagy would leave the Pact (declared 1 Nov). Khrushchev's own reasoning, recorded in Malin's notes, was that letting Hungary go would be read in London and Paris as weakness alongside Suez. Two mechanics follow. First, a patron's view of its satellites' seats should come through the political-domain penetration that already exists (satellites default to high patron coverage: Moscow had the AVH; Washington had SIFAR in Italy), and the embassy report is a dossier card with an AS-OF date and a verdict, not a raw number. Second, the propaganda payoff of a crush should scale with world attention: a concurrent war or Brink-band crisis divides the rival-street penalty (Suez cover), and a Calm-band crush at a moment of detente multiplies it (Prague 1968 damaged the Western CPs far more than Budapest because nothing else was happening). Both are readable from existing state: tension band and active wars.
findings.evidence: Malin notes, Presidium sessions of 30 and 31 Oct 1956 (CWIHP Bulletin 8-9); Andropov to the CPSU CC, 22-28 Oct 1956, in Csaba Bekes et al. (eds), The 1956 Hungarian Revolution: A History in Documents (2002); Gati (2006) ch. 5; the existing `Intel` political domain and CI_FLOOR_CLOSED/OPEN constants in crates/ugs-sim/src/intel.rs.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Three-seat country politics: GOVERNMENT, STREET, GUNS leans (-1000..1000 each) plus commitment DEPTH and a regime VALVE, with `alignment_of` derived from GOVERNMENT+DEPTH
mechanics_recommendations.why: This is the minimum granularity at which elections, coups and uprisings are different verbs with different preconditions, and it maps one-to-one onto every historical case researched; it reuses the existing OccupationZone popular-alignment scalar and the stability field, keeps the three-valued Alignment as a derived threshold so no downstream system changes, and adds no per-country special rules or AI.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Per country: `government: i16`, `street: i16`, `guns: i16`, `depth: Depth {Sympathetic, Aligned, Treaty, Satellite}`, `valve: GovernmentType {Democracy{next_election, cycle_months}, PartyState, Military}`. Monthly in TickSet::Politics: street drifts toward a target set by aid received, propaganda programs, the patron's recorded provocations (crushes, base incidents, aid cuts) and local economy (grain shortfalls and power constraints already computed); guns drift toward whoever supplies its arms (military stock grants, the arms-pipeline op); government moves only through valves and verbs. Divergence = |government - street| (and |government - guns|) scaled by (100 - stability) prints as a named condition: QUIET / RESTIVE / VOLATILE / RISING. The seat block is a BTreeMap<CountryTag, Seats>, digest-folded; existing event effects map without rewriting: SetAlignment sets the government seat to the pole's default value, AdjustStability stays stability, and a new AdjustSeat{country, seat, delta} effect joins the grammar. Read by the player as three words and a verdict per country in the paper's BLOC STANDINGS page, never as numbers. Decision changed: whether to spend a verb on a country before its valve date, and which seat to spend it on.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Scheduled election valve with a real calendar and pre-date verbs; coups and risings as unscheduled valves gated on GUNS and STREET divergence
mechanics_recommendations.why: Elections must be dates the player can see coming (UK 23 Feb 1950, Greece 5 Mar 1950, Turkey 14 May 1950, France June 1951, Italy June 1953) or they become HoI4's cosmetic events; coups and uprisings must be impossible without a real precondition or they become the HoI4 boost-ideology-then-coup exploit. Giving each valve a distinct trigger (date, army divergence, street divergence under a no-valve regime) makes the four influence verbs distinct because each one prepares a different valve.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Democracies carry `next_election` in data (sourced first dates, standard cycle).
