On the date, GOVERNMENT moves toward STREET by a fraction set by stability and incumbency, with a bounded roll from a `b"elections"` stream; covert party funding (an intel-network op, consuming the existing network strength and exposure) adds a bias and, if blown, a street backlash and a deniability spend; overt conditional aid (the Marshall 1948 verb) adds a bias only in Aligned-or-deeper countries and shifts the street against the patron by a small amount regardless. Coup: available to a rival only when |guns - government| exceeds a threshold and stability is below a threshold; success installs a Military valve with a legitimacy penalty and a government lean equal to guns. Rising: fires when street divergence exceeds a threshold in a PartyState or Military regime; it is not a player button, it is the state the patron then answers. AI democracies simply run the valve. Read by the player as a NEXT VALVE column ('ELECTION JUNE 1951', 'NONE: PARTY STATE', 'ARMY DECIDES') and wire notices when a country changes condition. Decision changed: where the two or three influence slots go this quarter, and whether to fund a party covertly or aid it overtly.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Asymmetric patron discipline verbs: planned patrons purge or garrison or crush; market patrons condition credits, supply or embargo arms, and go public; the crush itself reuses the occupation-zone machinery
mechanics_recommendations.why: The West disciplined allies through sterling, Bomarc press releases and the Johnson letter; the East through purges, Rokossovsky and armor. Putting the asymmetry in the discipline verb makes pillar 2's mirror an expression of pillar 4, and reusing OccupationZone (control, popular alignment, insurgency, garrison requirements, zone policy) means a crushed satellite is a state the sim already knows how to run, cost and rebel.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Planned patron on a Satellite-depth client: PURGE (drops guns and government divergence at a stability cost to the client, no tension, no world-opinion bill, available only pre-rising), GARRISON (assign divisions to the client, raising the crush option's odds and lowering street lean slowly), CRUSH (answer to a rising: the client's territory becomes an occupation zone held by the patron with alignment set from the street seat, garrisons drawn from real divisions, insurgency per the existing rules; a Kadar-style client government is installed with legitimacy penalty). Market patron on Treaty-depth-or-deeper clients: CONDITIONAL CREDITS (industry or stock grant tied to an election bias or a base retention, moves street slightly against the patron), ARMS SUPPLY / EMBARGO (moves guns toward or away from the patron; embargo opens the client to the rival's arms verb, the Pakistan 1965 effect), PUBLIC PRESSURE (a wire statement that can drop an allied government at the next valve, Diefenbaker 1963, at a street cost). Both patrons: TOLERATE a rising (accept a depth loss and a bloc-wide stability contagion, already in the corpus, and open the client to the rival's aid verb). Read by the player as the verb buttons on the embassy report card with the price printed in tension, legitimacy, divisions, credits and 'STREET REACTION' words. Decision changed: crush versus tolerate versus pre-empt, and for a market patron, whether to pay for compliance or accept a rung of drift.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: World-opinion payout as seat deltas in other countries, not a global scalar, with attention scaling and a delayed memory term
mechanics_recommendations.why: Hungary's real cost to Moscow was the CPGB losing a quarter of its members, Italian intellectuals leaving the PCI and Iceland reversing its base vote, i.e. the crusher's sympathizers in the rival bloc's streets shrinking; the state-level tension spike decayed within a season, as the tension meter already does. A global opinion number would be gamed and would not change any specific decision; seat deltas in named countries directly reduce the crusher's future election leverage there, which is a decision the player was already making. Suez cover and the 1956-1968-1980 escalation of revolts are both historical and cheap to model.
mechanics_recommendations.how: On CRUSH: every country whose street currently leans toward the crusher loses lean toward the crusher proportional to regime openness (the existing CI_FLOOR open/closed split doubles as a media-openness proxy) and to ideological proximity; the amount is divided when tension is in Crisis or Brink or a war is active (attention elsewhere) and multiplied in Calm. On TOLERATE: the rival gains an aid verb on the client and every Satellite-depth client of the same patron gains a small permanent divergence bonus (precedent). Memory: each crush adds to a per-country `crushed_count` that multiplies the next rising's severity and the garrison requirement; it never decays, which is the 1989 bill. Read by the player as named lines in the paper the month after ('ROME: COMMUNIST PARTY LOSES INTELLECTUALS OVER BUDAPEST', 'REYKJAVIK: BASE VOTE REVERSED') and as the STREET column in BLOC STANDINGS shifting in the other bloc. Decision changed: whether a crush is affordable this month given what it does to your position in the rival's contested democracies.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: BLOC STANDINGS page and embassy-report pull cards, with foreign seats filtered through political-domain penetration
mechanics_recommendations.why: House rules: no panel without a verb, monthly still display, decisions are pull, every output changes a decision, and what you see is what you believe. Moscow saw Hungary coming through Andropov; Washington saw Italy through SIFAR and the embassy; both had coverage, and both still had to decide under a deadline.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Newspaper section registry: BLOC STANDINGS lists every country at Aligned depth or deeper for both blocs plus the contested non-aligned: NAME | GOVT | STREET | GUNS | DEPTH | NEXT VALVE | verdict sentence ('POLAND: PARTY SPLIT, STREET RESTIVE, ARMY UNDER ROKOSSOVSKY: HOLDS WHILE THE GARRISON STAYS'). Own-bloc seats print at the patron's political penetration (embassy floor gives PARTIAL by default; funding a network in your own satellite, as the KGB and CIA did, gives EXTENSIVE); rival and neutral seats print through the same intel filter at two significant words, 'NO COVERAGE' otherwise. When a country changes condition (RESTIVE to VOLATILE, a valve within 90 days, a patron provocation logged), an EMBASSY REPORT card fires as an event with the verbs on it and a deadline; this is the only push, and it is budget-capped by the number of influence slots (3-4 standing programs plus the event stream), so a superpower sees roughly one to two bloc-domestic decisions per game-month and a small power sees its own three seats and nothing else. Standing programs (aid level per client 0-3, propaganda program on a region, arms pipeline) are set once and never upkept, exactly like network funding. Decision changed: which country gets a slot this quarter and which seat the verb targets.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Drift attributable to the patron's own decision log, and a Peking-line flag for Eastern drift after the split
mechanics_recommendations.why: Every satellite drift in the record began with a patron choice (de-Stalinize, reconcile with Tito, cancel the sample bomb, withdraw the garrison, raise the norms); making the sim compute drift from those recorded choices means the embassy report can name the cause and the player learns the mirror is theirs. After 1960 the destination for Eastern drift was often Beijing, not Belgrade, and routing aid sources and opinion payouts to the wrong rival breaks the Albania and Romania arcs the corpus already scripts.
mechanics_recommendations.how: A small table of patron provocations keyed on existing `OptionChosen`/`EventFired` stamps and sim facts: chose de-Stalinization (street divergence in all party-state satellites for N months), reconciled with a satellite's declared enemy (guns and government divergence in that satellite: Belgrade 1955 to Albania), cancelled a credit or arms contract (guns drift), withdrew all divisions from a satellite (crush option removed, government lean freer), imposed a settlement over a client's objection (existing war-termination case). Each contributes a named line to the dossier's cause list. The government seat of an Eastern-bloc country can carry a `pole: Moscow | Peking` marker set by the split chain; drift toward Peking keeps EasternBloc for basing and the market allocator but redirects patron verbs, aid sources and world-opinion payouts to China and strips Moscow's purge and crush verbs unless it garrisons. Read by the player as the 'WHY' line on the embassy report and as a small red marker on BLOC STANDINGS. Decision changed: whether a line shift at home (a Secret Speech, a detente summit) is worth the satellite it loosens.

pitfalls: Whack-a-mole: 226 countries times three seats becomes Vic3's fifty-state problem if any seat ever demands upkeep or if the standings page implies every RESTIVE row wants a click. Seats must drift on uniform rules with zero maintenance, verbs must be slot-capped (3-4 standing programs plus one op) and the only push is a budgeted embassy report card; regions are where you look, a capped portfolio is where you act.

Pay-to-flip coups: HoI4's boost-ideology-then-coup loop and Balance of Power's destabilize spam both come from a coup verb whose only precondition is money. A coup must require a real GUNS-vs-GOVERNMENT divergence and low stability that the player can read but cannot buy directly; arms supply moves the army slowly and visibly, and the outcome ladder (clean, junta with legitimacy debt, failed with exposure, failed with street backlash) is shown before commitment, never a percentage.

Replacing the three-valued Alignment instead of deriving it: bloc basing, patrons, red lines, the market allocator and map tinting all read `alignment_of`; if the seat model sets a different truth, the world-timeline corpus's 189 events (SetAlignment, AdjustStability) and the acid test break. Keep the accessor, make it a threshold over GOVERNMENT plus DEPTH, and map old effects onto seats.

World opinion as a global scalar: a single number is gamed, has no address, and changes no decision. The payout must land in named countries' street seats so it directly reduces the crusher's next election leverage, and it must be printed as country-named newspaper lines.

Crush with no delayed cost and tolerate with no cost: if crushing only spikes the decaying tension meter the correct play is always to crush, which is roughly what Moscow concluded until 1989; if tolerating is free the correct play is always to tolerate. Crush needs the never-decaying memory term and the rival-street payout; tolerate needs the credit bill, the precedent contagion and the rival gaining an aid verb.

Cosmetic elections: HoI4 elections fire an event and nothing depends on it. Election results must be the only way GOVERNMENT moves in a democracy, must be readable months ahead as a date, and must be what the player's pre-date verbs are for; otherwise the STREET seat is decoration.

Forgetting the second Eastern pole: routing every Eastern drift to Non-Aligned makes Albania and post-1964 Romania nonsense and gives China no domestic-mirror role after the split; at minimum a Peking-line marker on the government seat is needed so verbs and payouts route to the right rival.

Determinism and ordering: seat drift, valve rolls and opinion payouts iterate over all countries and must run in sorted CountryTag order from labeled forks (`b"elections"`, `b"coups"`, `b"risings"`) on new_month or on the valve date, never per tick and never from HashMap order; every seat and marker goes into the digest.

Superpowers escaping the mirror: the USA and USSR must have seats too (McCarthy-era street, the Presidium's own succession, the 1964 removal of Khrushchev already in the corpus), or the player's bloc has politics and the player does not; content review should forbid SetAlignment on superpowers but not seat deltas.
analysts.first_hour_test: In the founding January 1950 edition the player opens BLOC STANDINGS and reads their own bloc as three words and a verdict per member with a NEXT VALVE column. As the USA: UNITED KINGDOM, GOVT WESTERN, STREET WESTERN, GUNS LOYAL, TREATY, ELECTION 23 FEB 1950, verdict 'ATTLEE HOLDS, MAJORITY THIN'; FRANCE, GOVT WESTERN, STREET DIVIDED (OPPOSITION: PCF, HOSTILE), GUNS LOYAL, TREATY, ELECTION JUNE 1951, verdict 'THIRD FORCE GOVERNS A COUNTRY ONE QUARTER COMMUNIST'; ITALY the same with ELECTION 1953; TURKEY, GOVT WESTERN-LEANING, ALIGNED (not yet treaty), ELECTION 14 MAY 1950; YUGOSLAVIA listed under the contested column as NON-ALIGNED, GOVT TITO, GUNS LOYAL TO TITO, with an aid verb available. The player sets one standing program (credits to Italy at level 2, or nothing) and unpauses. On 23 February the paper's March edition reports the UK election on schedule with the government seat unchanged and the majority line updated; on 14 May the Turkish valve fires, the Democrat Party wins, and the June edition prints 'ANKARA: NEW GOVERNMENT SEEKS ALLIANCE, DEPTH RISES TOWARD TREATY', showing that an election can deepen alignment, not only threaten it. As the USSR the same page shows YUGOSLAVIA, DRIFTED, with the crush verb greyed out ('NO GARRISON, NO BORDER FORCES') and only the purge and propaganda verbs live; POLAND, GOVT MOSCOW-LINE, STREET RESTIVE, GUNS UNDER ROKOSSOVSKY, SATELLITE, NO VALVE, verdict 'HOLDS WHILE THE GARRISON STAYS'; and one embassy report card in the first quarter ('TITOISTS IN THE BULGARIAN PARTY: PURGE OR IGNORE') priced in the client's stability and legitimacy with no tension cost. The test passes if by June 1950 the player has taken at most three influence decisions, can say from the page alone which ally is most at risk and when, has seen one seat move because of something they did (the Italian credits showing as a STREET shift in the April edition, attributed by name), and has never touched a number or been interrupted by a row that did not carry a verb.

findings.title: Twilight Struggle is legible because contest is a designed subset, every country carries one printed price, and control is a derived state the board shows you
findings.detail: Twilight Struggle (GMT Games, 2005, Gupta & Matthews; Deluxe Edition 2009; Playdek digital 2016) puts exactly one visible variable per country (influence markers for each side), one printed constant (stability 1-5, which IS the coup price: die + ops - 2x stability), and one binary flag (battleground, marked distinctly on the board). Control is derived (influence >= stability + opponent influence) and the physical game's most common table complaint was doing that arithmetic by eye for 80+ countries; the digital edition auto-highlights control and players immediately called it the better board. Coups in battlegrounds cost DEFCON; coups elsewhere do not - so the escalation price of an influence verb is a legible rule, not a roll. Scoring is regional (presence / domination / control), so 'standing' is read per region, never as a raw count of flags. The lesson for UGS: the influence map must pre-declare which ~10-15 states are battlegrounds per era (weighted by population + industry + geography), show a derived control/depth state rather than making the player infer it, and price the escalation cost of a verb as a printed rule tied to the tension band.
findings.evidence: Twilight Struggle rules v2 (GMT, 2009) sections 6.3 Coup Attempts, 6.4 Realignment, 10.0 Scoring; BoardGameGeek forum threads 'Deluxe edition marker readability' (2009-10) and Playdek app reviews praising auto-control highlighting; designer commentary by Ananda Gupta on 'the game is opportunity cost' (Ludology podcast ep. on TS, 2012).

findings.title: Every capped-envoy system in the genre stopped whack-a-mole, and the ones players call boring failed because the slot did nothing, not because it was capped
findings.detail: EU4 (Paradox, 2013) diplomats: 2-4 envoys, Improve Relations ties one up as a standing commitment; players accepted the cap for a decade because each diplomat visibly buys an outcome. Stellaris 2.6 'Verne' with Federations (17 Mar 2020) added envoys assigned to Improve/Harm Relations, GalCom, federation; reception: zero-micro was praised, 'set and forget' was the complaint - the effect (+0.75 opinion/month) was too small to ever revisit. Victoria 3 (25 Oct 2022) makes Influence a capacity that standing pacts consume (per-country cost scaling with target rank); 1.7 Sphere of Influence (24 Jun 2024) added power blocs with Leverage and Lobbies. Terra Invicta (Pavonis, EA 26 Sep 2022) uses Control Points with per-CP cost as a hard nation-holding cap, and its councilor missions are the cautionary tale: capped councilors but per-turn re-assignment produced the 'councilor micro is not fun' Steam/forum refrain. Synthesis: cap standing commitments (slots), make each slot's effect large enough to change a verdict sentence within ~3 months, and never require re-issuing an order to keep it running.
findings.evidence: EU4 wiki 'Diplomat' and 'Improve relations'; Stellaris dev diary #163 'Envoys' (Jan 2020) and r/Stellaris threads 'envoys feel pointless' (2020-21); Victoria 3 dev diary #22 'Diplomacy' and 1.7 dev diaries on Power Blocs/Leverage (May-Jun 2024); Terra Invicta Steam reviews and Pavonis forum 'Too much councilor micromanagement' (Oct 2022-2023).

findings.title: HoI4's diplomacy screen and Terra Invicta's nation panel show what an unbudgeted influence UI does at 200+ countries: a list you scroll, verbs you spam, and exact opinion numbers with nothing to discover
findings.detail: HoI4 (Paradox, 2016): the diplomacy view is one row per country; Boost Party Popularity is a standing political-power drain per target; Stage Coup is gated on the target's ideology popularity and spawns a civil war. Community verdict for eight years: 'improve relations spam', 'boost popularity is too slow to be worth it', coups are 'click and wait'. La Resistance (1.9, Feb 2020) moved the 'Boost Ideology' knob onto operatives and made it worse (tedium threads). Its one praised element is the opinion tooltip: a signed, reasoned breakdown of why a country feels as it does. Terra Invicta's nation panel is the opposite pole: the public-opinion share bar per faction and the per-stat readout (Unrest, Cohesion, Democracy, GDP) are praised as legible; but opinion is exact and global-visible, so influence play is arithmetic, not intelligence. Both show ideology popularity as a per-tick slider - the 'watching a simulation' texture our econ house rules forbid. Lessons: the default view is a triage list, never the full roster; the breakdown ledger is mandatory; opinion must be an estimate, not a fact.
findings.evidence: HoI4 wiki 'Diplomacy' (Boost party popularity, Stage coup); Paradox forum 'Boost party popularity is useless' (2017) and 'Spy system too tedious' (Mar 2020); Terra Invicta wiki 'Nation' panel; Steam review corpus for TI (2022-23) - 'spreadsheet' both as praise and complaint.

findings.title: Victoria 3's diplomatic play proves a visible escalation countdown is loved and an opaque accumulator (Leverage) is hated - drift must be a signed ledger with named causes
findings.detail: Vic3's Diplomatic Play UI (1.0, 2022): two columns of backers, a maneuvers budget, sway offers with printed prices (obligations, treaty ports, money), and an escalation bar that fills toward war on a visible timer. Players praise being able to see who is backing whom and when the clock runs out; the durable complaints are (a) AI interest is unexplained ('why does Prussia care about Persia'), (b) sway obligations are consequences you cannot inspect later. Sphere of Influence (1.7, June 2024) added Leverage - a per-country accumulator from GDP share, trade, migration, and pacts - and the launch-week feedback was that leverage 'just goes up', its sources visible only in a hover tooltip and its thresholds surprising ('suddenly they left my bloc'). This is the exact failure our econ research named for Vic3 state constraints. For UGS the monthly alignment delta on every country must decompose into <=6 signed named terms (aid ratio, trade share, radio reach, proximity/bases, occupation/incidents, scripted event modifiers) printed inline in the dossier, with the largest gap templated into the verdict - the battle inspector's modifier ledger pattern applied to politics.
findings.evidence: Victoria 3 dev diary #22 (Diplomatic Plays, Mar 2022); Paradox forum 'Diplomatic plays: AI backing is a black box' (Nov 2022); Vic3 1.7 patch notes and forum feedback threads 'Leverage is opaque' (Jun-Jul 2024); docs/research/war-legibility.md principle 3 (signed sorted modifier ledger + one generated sentence).

findings.title: Balance of Power invented the verdict-before-you-act line and the influence-verb set; its opacity is the specific thing to fix
findings.detail: Balance of Power (Chris Crawford, Mindscape 1985; 1990 Edition 1988/89) shipped the influence verb set UGS's sketch lists almost verbatim: economic aid, military aid, aid to insurgents, intervention for government or insurgents, destabilization, diplomatic pressure, treaties - each priced in prestige and each able to provoke a crisis with a visible escalation ladder. Crawford's book (Balance of Power: International Politics as the Ultimate Global Game, Microsoft Press 1986) documents hidden variables (insurgency, 'Finlandization', government strength) and concedes the top complaint: crises arriving with no readable cause. The 1990 Edition's response was an advisory text layer - the game telling you, in prose, what a policy would probably provoke before you commit. Its country 'Closeup' printing government, alignment posture, and insurgency as words was the first political dossier in the genre. Take: the advisor sentence and closeup-as-document, ported to our teletype register; fix: every number that produces the sentence is inspectable in the same document.
findings.evidence: Crawford, Balance of Power (Microsoft Press, 1986), chapters on the model and on player reactions; Balance of Power: The 1990 Edition manual (Mindscape) - Advisory and Closeup screens; contemporaneous reviews in Computer Gaming World (Nov 1985; Feb 1990).

findings.title: How to state risk: Kent's estimative words with a published legend beat both naked percentages and vague bands; the failure arc is the content
findings.detail: Sherman Kent, 'Words of Estimative Probability' (Studies in Intelligence, 1964) mapped period language to ranges: almost certain (93% +/-6), probable (75% +/-12), chances about even (50% +/-10), probably not (30% +/-10), almost certainly not (7% +/-5). XCOM: Enemy Unknown (2012) is the canonical percentage betrayal (the 95% miss); CK3 (2020) shows scheme success % with a visible contributor list and separate secrecy % and is broadly trusted because the inputs are on screen; Into the Breach (2018) removes the roll and previews outcomes exactly. The espionage readup already adopts outcome ladders with estimative words (principle 5). The refinement for coups: (1) print the ladder of named world-states, (2) label each rung with a Kent word, (3) print ONE legend, once, in the panel footer, giving the Kent ranges - 'honest bands' - so the player is never lied to and never sees '73%' either, (4) list the inspectable inputs beside it (ARMY LEAN, NETWORK STRENGTH, STABILITY, TARGET CI, TENSION BAND, PREP MONTHS). Failure then plays as the U-2 arc from the espionage doc: same-day wire flash with facts unclear, cover-story choice before evidence is known, attribution UNATTRIBUTED -> SUSPECTED -> PROVEN by named objects, and the next month's paper as the reckoning.
findings.evidence: Kent (1964), CIA CSI reprint; XCOM 'hit chance' Reddit/Firaxis commentary (2012-13); CK3 dev diary #16 'Schemes' (Jun 2020); docs/research/espionage.md principles 5-7; docs/design/systems/espionage.md 'Operation lifecycle'.

findings.title: Epistemic texture is the pillar's differentiator: no shipped influence system makes opinion an estimate, and the codebase already has the unused political intel domain to do it
findings.detail: HoI4, Terra Invicta, Vic3, and Twilight Struggle all show alignment/opinion as public truth. Our house rule (econ principle 6; war-legibility principle 5) is that foreign figures are estimates at two significant figures, sampled once per month, with coverage grade and AS-OF date. `Intel.penetration.political` is stored and today feeds only the crisis resolve band - it is the natural width source for the alignment bracket. The historical model is the CIA's own record: the Korea surprise (25 Jun 1950), the misread of Arbenz's army loyalty in 1954 that PBSuccess only survived because of a manufactured broadcast, and the 1958 misjudgment of Guinea (Washington's aid 'still in committee' while Moscow's credits landed). The rival's commitments are the second estimate: aid delegations and trade treaties are public (the Sino-Soviet treaty of 14 Feb 1950 printed its $300M credit in Pravda), radio is audible, party funding and coup preparation are not - so provenance differs per verb. War in the Pacific's claimed-vs-confirmed pattern applies: public commitments are exact, covert ones are ranges or '?' below a coverage threshold.
findings.evidence: crates/ugs-sim/src/intel.rs (DomainPenetration.political; consumer list in docs/design/systems/espionage.md table); docs/research/economic-agency.md principle 6; docs/research/war-legibility.md principle 5; Immerman, The CIA in Guatemala (1982); Wikipedia 'Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance'; assets/data/scenario/1950/events/07-sub-saharan-africa-1950-.ron 'guinea-courts-moscow'.

findings.title: The historical decision cadence for influence was a handful of large commitments per year - which is the decision budget
findings.detail: Jan-Jun 1950 alone contains the whole verb set at real dates: Sino-Soviet treaty and credit (14 Feb 1950 - an inherited Soviet aid commitment before the first move, the Volga-Don pattern); UK general election (23 Feb), Greek election (5 Mar), Turkish election with the Democrat Party landslide (14 May), Belgian election and Japanese House of Councillors (4 Jun); Truman's 'Campaign of Truth' speech (20 Apr 1950) unlocking the propaganda verb; the Act for International Development (Point Four) signed 5 Jun 1950 unlocking a standing aid slot; Radio Free Europe's first broadcast (4 Jul 1950). Later anchors: Italy 1948 (~$1M+ covert party funding, the election-support template), Philippines 1951/1953 (Lansdale, NAMFREL, Magsaysay), Iran (Aug 1953), Guatemala (Jun 1954), Guinea (Oct 1958 -> Soviet $35M credit 1959), Bandung (18-24 Apr 1955) as the Non-Aligned pole's birth. Washington ran perhaps 3-6 major standing programs and 1-2 active covert political ops at any time; Moscow fewer. A budget of ~1-2 influence decisions per game-month (from 3 standing slots + 1 active-op slot in 1950, growing by unlock events to ~6+2 by 1960) matches history and keeps the cross-pillar total near 6/month.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia: 'Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance', '1950 United Kingdom general election', '1950 Greek legislative election', '1950 Turkish general election', 'Campaign of Truth', 'Point Four Program', 'Radio Free Europe'; Mistry, The United States, Italy and the Origins of Cold War (2014); Wilford, The Mighty Wurlitzer (2008); docs/research/economic-agency.md principle 3.

findings.title: What the codebase gives the slice for free, and the three seams it must respect
findings.detail: (1) `Alignment` is three-valued and every downstream read goes through `Military::alignment_of` - a fine axis (-1000..1000, the same scale `OccupationZone.alignment` already uses) must PROJECT onto the enum by thresholds so bloc basing, patrons, the market allocator, and map tinting keep working; the projection thresholds are what the standings ledger counts. (2) Stability is dynamic per country (u8, `AdjustStability`), `legitimacy` exists as world-opinion currency, and `NationMeta` carries leader/government/situation only for 1950 sovereigns - the 37 newborn states have no meta, so the dossier header must degrade to 'PROVISIONAL GOVERNMENT' without a portrait. (3) AI countries resolve choice events by option 0 at the deadline (`events.rs`), which is why decolonization is a script: the contest becomes real only if a newborn's option choice weights the standing commitments both blocs hold on it. (4) The region dossier (`econ_ui.rs refresh_dossier`) is the template: header, blocks, verdict footer in severity color, verb buttons with tooltips that state cost and the verdict they answer, disabled verbs printing why. (5) `paper_ui` sections are an array of functions with an 'influence standings' page reserved; `Construction.log` + `RegionSnapshots.wire` are the heartbeat pattern; `GreatProjectDef.payload Influence(i32)` is logged-but-unused and should become a commitment payout.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: INFLUENCE map mode: hue = alignment axis, saturation = commitment depth, markers = contests, hatch = no coverage
mechanics_recommendations.why: The map is where the player looks; it must answer 'where is the world moving and where can I act' at a glance without 226 tooltips. Twilight Struggle's board works because contest is a marked subset; HoI4's political map fails because it paints only the government's current label.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Paint each country's provinces on a diverging hue (Western blue <-> Eastern red, with Non-Aligned as a third distinct olive/ochre hue once the country's position sits in the middle band) at saturation stepped by depth (SYMPATHETIC pale -> ALIGNED -> TREATY -> SATELLITE full). Overlay three marker kinds, drawn only for the designed battleground subset (top ~12-15 by population+industry+geography weight per era) and any country with an open contest: a pulsing pip like the battle marker for CONTESTED (both blocs hold commitments or a coup/election window is open), a small clock glyph with 'ELECTION 4 MO' for scheduled contests, and an arrow glyph for countries whose last-month delta crossed a threshold. Countries below LIMITED political coverage render desaturated with a diagonal hatch and no marker ('as you believe it'). Colonial territories take the parent's hue at low saturation with no scripted dates leaked. Colorblind pass: red/blue diverge plus the third hue must survive deuteranopia; depth is also readable as saturation steps, and battleground status as the marker, never color alone. Selecting a country opens the political dossier - the map mode never shows a number.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: The Standings ledger (panel + newspaper page): triage list by default, full roster on demand, bloc totals weighted three ways
mechanics_recommendations.why: House rule 3: regions are where you look, a capped portfolio is where you act - at 226 countries the default view must be a triage list of <=12 rows. Victory checkpoints read this ledger, so it is also the score.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Panel (key P, `UGS_PANEL=politics`): header strip WEST 41 / EAST 12 / NON-ALIGNED 19 (Δ +1 / 0 / -1 this month) in three columns - STATES, POPULATION, INDUSTRY - because counting Luxembourg equal to India is a bug. Default tab BATTLEGROUNDS: rows COUNTRY | POSITION (axis glyph with bracket) | DEPTH | TREND (arrow + largest cause word) | NEXT (ELECTION MAY 1950 / COUP WINDOW / INDEPENDENCE MOVEMENT / --) | OURS (your commitments, exact) | THEIRS (estimate at 2 sig figs, '?' below coverage) | COVERAGE grade. Filter chips: BATTLEGROUNDS (default), MY BLOC (the domestic mirror), NEWBORN (states born <24 months), CONTESTS <=6 MO, ALL (the 226 roster, sortable, explicitly the last chip). Second tab COMMITMENTS: your slots as cards (target, verb, monthly flow, since-date, effect this month), 3/4 used. The newspaper's reserved page prints the header strip, the top-5 movers with cause, nations born this month with their first-month lean, and 'FOREIGN COMMITMENTS ARE ESTIMATES' in the footer - frozen for the month.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: The Political Dossier: a one-page teletype document with a computed verdict sentence, sibling of the region dossier and battle inspector
mechanics_recommendations.why: No panel without a verb; the unit of legibility is a computed sentence; every row terminates in a button or an inline why. Balance of Power's closeup plus the battle inspector's modifier ledger, in one fixed form.
mechanics_recommendations.how: HEADER: display name, government and leader from NationMeta (newborns print 'PROVISIONAL GOVERNMENT'), stability band word, and the AXIS STRIP: a 21-notch horizontal line with your best-estimate marker and a bracket whose width comes from political penetration (LIMITED = +/-4 notches, EXTENSIVE = +/-1), sampled at month rollover, stamped 'AS OF MAR 1950 - COVERAGE PARTIAL'; depth printed beside it. INSTITUTIONS block (the per-faction answer, v1 as a fixed tuple, never a list): ARMY / GOVERNMENT / STREET, each with a lean glyph (W / E / N) and grip pips 1-5; these are what verbs target (coups need ARMY lean, elections move by STREET lean, aid moves GOVERNMENT). PRESSURES block: the signed monthly drift ledger, <=6 terms, each named with its source (US AID +3 / SOVIET CREDIT -1 / RFE REACH +1 / SOVIET BORDER -2 / OCCUPATION INCIDENT -1 / EVENT: BAGHDAD PACT +2), foreign terms bracketed as estimates. NEXT block: the scheduled contest (election date, or 'NO SCHEDULED CONTEST - MILITARY REGIME'). FOOTER verdict, grammar STATE DIRECTION: DOMINANT CAUSE; KEY INSTITUTION; NEXT CONTEST - e.g. 'ALIGNMENT DRIFTING WEST: US AID 3x SOVIET (EST); ARMY LOYAL TO GOVERNMENT; ELECTION IN 4 MONTHS' or 'SATELLITE RESTIVE: STREET LEANS AWAY; ARMY LOYAL; STABILITY 41'. Verb buttons beside it, each tooltip stating price, slot use, and which verdict it answers; disabled verbs print why ('NO NETWORK - FUND ONE IN INTELLIGENCE', 'NO FREE COMMITMENT SLOT', 'BLOCKED: TENSION BAND BRINK').

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Capped commitment slots with two price shapes: standing programs as monthly flows, operations as one-shot spends of network and deniability
mechanics_recommendations.why: Decision count is a designed budget; envoy-cap precedents work when the slot matters; history ran a handful of large programs. Standing flows compete with projects for the same construction pool, which makes influence a guns-vs-butter-vs-friends choice inside pillar 4.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Two slot kinds per country. STANDING slots (USA/SOV: 3 at start, +1 at the Korea/NSC-68 funding step-change event, +1 at 1955; UK/FRA 2; other majors 1; minors 0-1): AID PROGRAM (centi/month from the construction pool, tiers 1-3; the RATIO to the rival's aid is what moves GOVERNMENT lean - Guinea's lesson), MISSIONS & RADIO (near-free in cash, occupies a slot, moves STREET lean slowly, jammed by target counterintel; unlocked for the US by the Campaign of Truth event 20 Apr 1950, RFE 4 Jul 1950), PARTY SUPPORT (standing covert funding through an existing intel network; deniability-exposed). One ACTIVE-OP slot (two by 1955): ELECTION PUSH (one-shot spend at a scheduled contest: lump cash + network strength; resolves on election day through the espionage op machinery), BACK THE ARMY / coup (network strength above a threshold + deniability; multi-month prep with clean abort; resolves via `b"op-resolve"`), and inside your own bloc TIGHTEN (crackdown: +grip, -alignment, legitimacy debit and a propaganda term the rival gains for 12 months) and SUBSIDIZE (aid to a satellite). Standing programs never decay or need re-issuing; if the target flips against you or expels advisers, the program auto-suspends with a wire line and frees the slot - orphans are impossible. The COMMITMENTS tab shows n/cap; a full portfolio is the normal state and dropping one is the decision. Great Project `Influence(i32)` payloads land as a temporary PRESSURES term on the host country.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Risk stated as an outcome ladder with Kent words and one published legend; failure as a three-week wire arc that ends in the newspaper
mechanics_recommendations.why: Percentages get disbelieved (XCOM); vague bands feel like lies; Kent's language with honest ranges is period-correct and inspectable. Failure must be content that changes standings, not a modifier.
mechanics_recommendations.how: The AUTHORIZE card for a coup or election push prints: the rungs CLEAN FLIP / FLIP WITH EVIDENCE / QUIET FIZZLE / EXPOSED FAILURE / CIVIL WAR, each with a Kent word (PROBABLE / CHANCES ABOUT EVEN / UNLIKELY ...), the posture dial (cautious/standard/aggressive) re-labeling the rungs live, and the inputs that produced them as a short signed list (ARMY LEAN W+2, NETWORK 62, STABILITY 38, TARGET CI HIGH, TENSION WARY, PREP 3 MO). The panel footer carries the one legend: 'PROBABLE ~75% (63-87), ABOUT EVEN ~50% ...' - printed once, never per rung. On failure: day 0 wire flash naming a place and a fact ('TEHRAN: TANKS IN THE STREETS; SITUATION CONFUSED'); a cover-story choice event with a deadline before evidence is known; attribution moves UNATTRIBUTED -> SUSPECTED -> PROVEN by named objects (captured radio, a talking colonel, a defector); the target country's PRESSURES gain a 'BLOWN OPERATION' term against you and its neighbors gain a smaller one (the Guatemala effect on Latin American opinion); legitimacy and deniability debit; tension spikes per the existing blown-op rule. Next month's paper leads with it - your own masthead printing the cover story (the party organ calls it an imperialist provocation; the broadsheet prints 'STATE DEPARTMENT DENIES'), which is how the player reads their own lie.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Epistemic texture: true alignment vs the embassy estimate, rival commitments by provenance, and wrongness the player chose
mechanics_recommendations.why: What you see is what you believe is the house signature; the political intel domain exists with no political consumer; every other game shows opinion as truth and so has nothing for spies to find.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Sim state holds true axis position, depth, and institution leans. The UI computes the estimate once per month from political penetration: bracket width and a deterministic offset sampled from a display-side stream (never jittering between rollovers), rounded to notch resolution. Own bloc members and countries where you hold a standing program get near-exact reads (the program is itself a source - a reason to keep one). Rival commitments print by provenance: public treaties and announced credits are exact and stamped PUBLIC; radio reach is observable; covert party funding and coup prep appear only above PARTIAL coverage as '?' -> 'SUSPECTED' -> a range, stamped with a provenance line ('EMBASSY REPORTING', 'AGENT NETWORK', 'PRESS'). Diegetic tells below coverage: the paper's world-events column still prints public facts (a Soviet trade delegation arriving in Conakry) so a low-coverage battleground is never a black hole, just an unquantified one. Every foreign figure sits next to its coverage grade so a surprise flip (Korea-style) is a coverage state the player tolerated, not a lie. Reveals happen through existing intel events: an EXTENSIVE-coverage upgrade rewrites the bracket and prints 'REVISED: TEHRAN ARMY LEAN NOW ASSESSED EAST'.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: The monthly heartbeat: 3-6 wire lines with cause, a briefing card with one recommendation, and pull-only contests
mechanics_recommendations.why: Date-stamped still display with a curated heartbeat is the house cadence; decisions are pull not push; scheduled contests are the natural pull because they have dates.
mechanics_recommendations.how: At rollover, rank candidate lines by (bloc-weight of the country x |delta| x battleground flag), cap at 6, each line naming a country and its dominant cause: 'GHANA DRIFTS EAST - SOVIET CREDITS OUTWEIGH POINT FOUR 3:1 (EST)', 'TURKEY: DEMOCRAT PARTY WINS - ANKARA DEPTH ALIGNED -> TREATY OFFERED', 'IRAN: ARMY LEAN NOW WEST (YOUR NETWORK, 4TH MONTH)', 'HUNGARY: STREET RESTIVE - STABILITY 44'. The briefing card (top of the politics panel, and the paper's page) prints the standings strip, the three most contested battlegrounds with their NEXT dates, COMMITMENTS n/cap, and exactly one templated recommendation derived only from visible data ('RECOMMEND: ELECTION PUSH IN TURKEY - CONTEST IN 2 MONTHS, STREET LEANS WEST, ACTIVE-OP SLOT FREE') so the player can learn to beat it. Pull events: an election is announced on the wire 6 months out (no popup); an independence event fires as it does today but its option choice for an AI newborn is weighted by the standing commitments each bloc holds on the parent territory in the 24 months before - the contest opens BEFORE birth, read on the parent's dossier as 'INDEPENDENCE MOVEMENT: ACTIVE - LEANS EAST (EST)' without a date; results with your money in them (election day, coup resolution) are the only popups.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: The domestic mirror in the same form: your bloc's members appear in the MY BLOC chip with the identical dossier and two verbs
mechanics_recommendations.why: The sketch's mirror (satellites drift, allies elect unfriendly governments, crackdowns cost world opinion) needs no new surface if the dossier is one form; Yugoslavia 1948 and Finland are in the 1950 start as worked examples.
mechanics_recommendations.how: MY BLOC rows sort by threat (depth falling, stability low, contest near). A satellite dossier verdict reads 'SATELLITE RESTIVE: STREET LEANS AWAY; ARMY LOYAL; STABILITY 41' with verbs SUBSIDIZE (a standing aid slot spent inside your bloc - the opportunity cost is a battleground you cannot fund) and TIGHTEN (a one-shot: +grip and depth for 12 months, -STREET lean, legitimacy debit, and a named 'CRACKDOWN' pressure term the rival's radio amplifies in every neighboring country - the 1956 texture, playable in 1953 East Berlin). An ally's election appears with 'ELECTION IN 3 MO - UNFRIENDLY PARTY LEADS'; ELECTION PUSH is legal against allies but its exposure rung costs depth with that ally specifically (Italy 1948 done badly). Yugoslavia at start reads 'LOST SATELLITE: DEPTH HOSTILE-NA; TIGHTEN UNAVAILABLE - NO BORDER GARRISON' as the USSR's tutorial row; Finland reads 'FINLANDIZED: NEUTRAL BY TREATY'. Losing a member to a drift you could read for six months is the pillar's fair failure.

pitfalls: Shipping the map mode and dossier before the verbs: house rule 1 says an inspector alone worsens the watching-a-simulation complaint; the v1 slice must ship at least AID PROGRAM and ELECTION PUSH with the dossier in the same commit.

Letting the default view be the 226-row roster (HoI4's diplomacy list): the ALL chip must be the last tab, and every standing figure in the ledger must be monthly and date-stamped - per-tick alignment sliders in a list are the exact texture the econ research banned.

Uncapped or meaningless slots: if a standing program cannot change a verdict sentence within ~3 months on a battleground, the player will set-and-forget it (Stellaris envoys) and the pillar reads as flavor; conversely, if slot count scales with country count, whack-a-mole returns.

Printing a single success percentage on coups (XCOM betrayal) OR printing bands with no legend (feels like the UI is hiding a die); the Kent-word ladder with one published range legend is the honest middle.

Leaking scripted futures through the UI: the timeline fires Ghana on 6 Mar 1957 by data; the colonial dossier must never print the date - only an assessed 'INDEPENDENCE MOVEMENT: ACTIVE' with a coverage grade, or the player learns the script instead of reading the world.

Estimates without tells: a low-coverage country whose true lean differs from the bracket must still emit public wire facts (delegations, treaties, election results) or a flip reads as a bug rather than as intelligence the player declined to buy.

Newborn states with no NationMeta (37 of them) rendering a broken header, and the fine axis failing to project onto the three-valued `Alignment` enum - every downstream read (bloc basing, patrons, market allocator, map tinting) goes through `alignment_of` and must see the projected value.

Color-only encoding on the influence map: red/blue plus a third hue and saturation steps must be checked for deuteranopia, with battleground/contested status carried by markers and hatch, never by color alone.
Letting the domestic mirror become a second panel: bloc members are a filter chip in the same ledger and the same dossier form, or the decision budget doubles silently.
analysts.first_hour_test: Playing the USA from 1 Jan 1950 at speed 3 (roughly a real minute per game-month unpaused, with pauses), the player must do all of the following before 1 Jul 1950 and see each one graded by a document. Minute 0-5: press the INFLUENCE map mode and see a world painted by alignment hue and depth saturation with about a dozen pulsing battleground pips (Iran, Greece, Turkey, Italy, Guatemala, Indonesia, Indochina among them) and hatched no-coverage countries; open the politics panel and read the standings strip (WEST / EAST / NON-ALIGNED by states, population, industry), a BATTLEGROUNDS triage list of about twelve rows with NEXT dates already visible (UK ELECTION 23 FEB - NO STAKE, GREECE ELECTION 5 MAR, TURKEY ELECTION 14 MAY, GUATEMALA ELECTION NOV), and COMMITMENTS 0/3. Minute 5-15: click Iran, read a one-page dossier whose footer says something like 'LEANING WEST, DRIFTING: BRITISH OIL DISPUTE -2; ARMY LOYAL TO SHAH; STREET LEANS NATIONALIST; NO SCHEDULED CONTEST', with the axis bracket stamped 'AS OF JAN 1950 - COVERAGE PARTIAL' and the Soviet column reading '?'; start an AID PROGRAM (tier 1) and watch the pool draw appear as a standing flow in the econ panel too. Minute 15-25: the February paper prints the Sino-Soviet treaty as a PUBLIC Soviet commitment to Peking with its credit figure, and the March paper prints a Greece result line with a cause; Truman's Campaign of Truth event fires on 20 Apr and the wire says a MISSIONS & RADIO slot has opened - the player assigns it to Iran or Italy. Minute 25-40: the May rollover carries 'TURKEY: DEMOCRAT PARTY WINS - ANKARA DEPTH ALIGNED -> TREATY OFFERED' as the top wire line and the Iran dossier's PRESSURES ledger now shows 'US AID +3 (2ND MONTH)' with the verdict changed from DRIFTING to HOLDING - the player has seen their own commitment change a sentence. Minute 40-60: the June briefing card prints COMMITMENTS 2/3 and one recommendation derived from visible rows; Point Four's signing (5 Jun) opens the third slot, and the player has a real choice between Guatemala (election in November, STREET leans left) and Indochina (a French war, no contest) before the Korea flash on 25 Jun. Mirror check as the USSR in the same window: slot 1 is already occupied by the Sino-Soviet credit before the first move, Yugoslavia reads as a lost satellite with TIGHTEN unavailable, and the same Turkey line reads as a loss with a Soviet cause word. The pillar is playable if, by the Korea event, the player can name one country they moved, one they are losing and why, and one contest they are saving a slot for - and if none of that required opening more than three documents.

findings.title: Alignment is already dynamic and has exactly one read API; pillar 2 should own the value BEHIND Military::alignment_of, not replace the API
findings.detail: The three-valued bloc (ugs_data::Alignment, crates/ugs-data/src/lib.rs:61-66) lives as a 1950 baseline in CountryDef (lib.rs:68-82) with a runtime override map `Military.alignments` (crates/ugs-sim/src/military.rs:324-333) read through `Military::alignment_of` (military.rs:367-378), digest-folded (military.rs:717-720). Every downstream behavior already keys off that accessor: bloc basing / theater painting (`friendly_soil`, military.rs:540-574), patrons (`patrons_of`, settlement.rs:453-465), same-side checks (settlement.rs:558-568), red lines (settlement.rs:505-528), the nuclear patron ultimatum (nuclear.rs:597-604), and the newspaper masthead (paper_ui.rs:178-190). world-timeline.md states the rule: no system reads CountryDef.alignment directly. The integration-minimal design is therefore: a new `Influence` resource holds a fine-grained per-country position (i16, -1000 East .. +1000 West, same unit as OccupationZone.alignment at settlement.rs:117-135), and a single helper `Influence::set_position(&mut self, &mut Military, tag, value)` writes BOTH the position and the projected band into `military.alignments` atomically (WesternBloc if pos >= +BAND_GATE, EasternBloc if <= -BAND_GATE, else NonAligned). Zero call sites change; `alignment_of` stays instant (no waiting for a monthly projection); Influence is authoritative and `Military.alignments` is its cache. This mirrors how Twilight Struggle (GMT Games, 2005) keeps one number per country (influence points) and derives 'control' from a threshold, rather than storing control as independent state.

findings.title: Scripted content overwrites bloc 29 times and nothing can pull back; Independence never touches alignment at all — newborn states inherit a static data default
findings.detail: `EventEffect::SetAlignment` (ugs-data lib.rs:265-270) is applied as a hard `military.alignments.insert` (events.rs:210-218): Cuba, Guatemala, Ghana, Guinea, Indonesia, Egypt, Hungary, Albania, Pakistan, Japan, PRC etc. (grep count: 1+6+3+1+4+3+4+7 = 29 uses across assets/data/scenario/1950/events/*.ron). The `Independence` effect (events.rs:228-297) transfers provinces, region ownership, manpower and prints 'THE COLD WAR HAS A NEW BATTLEGROUND, AND BOTH BLOCS KNOW IT' — but sets no alignment; the newborn's bloc is whatever `countries/independence.ron` says (18 WesternBloc, 18 NonAligned, 1 EasternBloc). Only Ghana has a follow-on chain that decides its course (`ghana-pan-african-course`, EventFired 642 days after `ghana-independence`, three SetAlignment options). The fix that preserves the corpus and the acid test (`the_world_turns_to_1970` asserts Cuba EasternBloc at events.rs:1003-1008): keep `SetAlignment` as a 'band-edge shove' (position := clamp into the named band at its near edge plus a margin, no-op if already there), add `ShiftAlignment { country, delta }` and `LockAlignment { country, months }` effects, and make `Independence` seed the newborn at baseline_pole * NEWBORN_SEED (e.g. +/-150, inside the NonAligned band) with a `contested_until = tick + 36 months` window. After the shove the tug-of-war continues, which is the sketch's 'scripted timing, unscripted outcomes'. Historical anchor: Ghana's 'positive neutralism' (All-African Peoples' Conference, Accra, Dec 1958) was a course Nkrumah chose under competing offers (Volta River aid from the US/World Bank vs Soviet/Chinese courtship), not a birth attribute — Westad, The Global Cold War (2005), ch. 4.

findings.title: Espionage v1 already IS the covert delivery layer for coups and election interference; pillar 2 must consume it, not duplicate it
findings.detail: intel.rs resolves queued ops in a single path (intel.rs:418-515): a network per (owner,target) with `OP_MIN_STRENGTH = 40` gate (intel.rs:51), `OP_STRENGTH_COST = 25` spend (intel.rs:53), a blown roll `OP_BLOWN_BASE + ci/4 + tension_band*40` from the `b"op-resolve"` stream (intel.rs:446-450), deniability spend and doubled tension when deniability < 40 (intel.rs:499-505), and a 'COVERT ACTION EXPOSED' standing grievance notice. The commands are player-gated (`if let Some(owner) = player.0.clone()`, command.rs:823-837). espionage.md 'Deferred sequencing' explicitly says 'Coups/election ops arrive with the influence pillar and consume this layer' (docs/design/systems/espionage.md:186-190) and the research readup rules are binding: networks never decay from inaction, upkeep is never a player job, outcome ladders not percentages, decisions are pull not push (docs/research/espionage.md:13-51). Integration: `SponsorCoup` and `BackElection` become arms of an `InfluenceOp` enum resolved in influence.rs, but they read `intel.networks[(owner,target)].strength`, spend it with the same constants, roll from their own labeled forks, and on 'blown' call the same deniability/tension/notice code (factor intel.rs:499-514 into a `pub fn blow(&mut Intel, ...)` helper). Aid and Presence (propaganda) do NOT go through networks — they are overt and safe, which is what differentiates the verbs. The Political domain penetration (intel.rs:89-94, `NET_CAP_POLITICAL = 650`) is the natural fuzz width for how precisely the player sees a foreign country's position ('as you believe it', newspaper.md).

findings.title: Two existing currencies already mean 'world opinion' and 'popular consent'; the country position should share their unit and the legitimacy ledger should be the price of crushing uprisings
findings.detail: `Settlements.legitimacy: BTreeMap<CountryTag, i32>` (settlement.rs:256, accessor :281) is written by events (`GrantLegitimacy`, events.rs:207-209), war-aim upgrades (command.rs:546) and Exploitation zone policy (-1/month, settlement.rs:1355-1358), and spent on high-sovereignty clauses (settlement.rs:745-748, 1036-1042). `OccupationZone.alignment: i16` (-1000..1000, settlement.rs:117-135) already drifts monthly by policy (`ALIGN_DRIFT_MILGOV = -8`, `ALIGN_DRIFT_CLIENT = 6`, `ALIGN_DRIFT_EXPLOIT = -20`, settlement.rs:62-64, applied :1345-1352) and gates incorporation at 400 (:67). So pillar 2 needs no new 'world opinion' number: a Hungary-1956 style option that crushes an uprising should cost legitimacy and lock the satellite; a blown coup should cost legitimacy in addition to deniability and tension. The country position uses the same -1000..1000 i16 scale so zone alignment can flow into the country position when a zone ends (treaty Restore/ClientState) — one unit, one mental model for the player ('alignment' means the same thing on the occupation card and the influence map). Economy readup house rule applies: the unit of legibility is a verdict sentence, never raw permille (docs/research/economic-agency.md:18-52).

findings.title: Treaty clauses ClientState and Neutralization are toothless today and war-termination.md assigns their teeth to this pillar
findings.detail: When a settlement signs, `Clause::ClientState { state, patron }` only writes a war-log line ('ENTERS ORBIT BY TREATY', settlement.rs:970-975) and `Clause::Neutralization` only inserts into `settlements.neutralized` (settlement.rs:987), a set read nowhere except the digest (settlement.rs:430; grep confirms no other reads in sim or app). war-termination.md 'Implementation deviations' says: 'Neutralization and ClientState clauses are recorded with wire notices; their mechanical teeth (basing exclusion, orbit effects) land with the influence pillar' and 'Unrecognized-holding alignment drift toward the rival bloc awaits the influence system' (docs/design/systems/war-termination.md:341-351). Integration: ClientState => `set_position(state, patron_pole_band_edge)` + `LockAlignment(state, TRUCE_MONTHS)`; Neutralization => `set_position(state, 0)` + lock (Austria 1955: the corpus's austrian-state-treaty event already SetAlignment NonAligned + legitimacy +15). Because the lock lives in Influence and `friendly_soil` reads the projected band, neutralized states automatically exclude foreign basing with no extra code. Also `settlement::evaluate` (settlement.rs:602+) should read the target's position when pricing a ClientState clause: dragging a +600 Western state into Moscow's orbit should be far dearer than one at -100.

findings.title: The AI precedent is a published deterministic allocator, not a planner: reuse the market-investment allocator shape and the 'skip the player' loop pattern
findings.detail: planning.rs:337-378 is the template: per-market-country monthly pass, deterministic integer score per region (grid factor/10 + urban/10 + ZONE_BONUS - tax drag), largest-remainder split of a budget, attribution recorded (`construction.attribution`) so the dossier can print 'where capital went and why'. economic-agency.md's AI note (docs/design/systems/economic-agency.md:165-171) is 'zero new AI code'; settlement.rs:1176-1200 and military.rs:1546-1560 show the only AI pattern in the codebase: iterate in BTreeMap order, `if player.0.as_ref() == Some(me) { continue }`. Influence AI = one monthly allocator per bloc leader (USA, SOV; PRC once the split fires), budget = f(`Economies.industry[leader].actual_centi`, planning.rs:77-80), targets = every country with |position| < LOCK band and not locked, score = population (Demographics.provinces, demography.rs:61-64, summed by current holder) x contestedness (1000 - |position|) x newborn-window multiplier x 'rival active here last month' multiplier; spend top-K by largest remainder, record `attribution[(sponsor,target)]`. Both leaders read LAST month's snapshot of positions (double-buffer) so USA-then-SOV order is not load-bearing — the same reasoning as the deterrence-reads-last-month comment at events.rs:116-122. The published formula becomes a newspaper line ('MOSCOW'S CHEQUEBOOK THIS MONTH: INDONESIA, EGYPT, GHANA'). Precedents: Twilight Struggle's official solo bot priorities (GMT, 'Twilight Struggle: Red Tide' 2021 and the community 'TS bot' cards) are published priority lists; Terra Invicta (Pavonis Interactive, 2022) shows faction control-point priorities in the UI.

findings.title: Determinism plumbing: every new resource must touch three registries, seed on the first tick, use constant RNG labels and month flags — and the savegame digest already omits Intel/Crises/Deterrence/Nuclear
findings.detail: A new `Influence` resource must be (a) inserted in `SimPlugin::build` (lib.rs:103-120), (b) reset in `savegame::reset_sim` (savegame.rs:58-85), and (c) folded into the replay digest (savegame.rs:136-155). Note (c) currently digests only Demographics, Economies, Agriculture, Military, Settlements, RegionalIndustry, Construction, EconomyStatic, FiredEvents — NOT Intel (which has its own `digest`, intel.rs:201-237), Crises, Deterrence or NuclearPrograms; the replay test would not catch an influence-op divergence unless Influence (and ideally Intel) are added. Scenario data is inserted after plugin build in every harness (`app.insert_resource(SimScenario(...))`, events.rs:568-577), so per-country seeding must use the first-tick `seeded` flag pattern (intel.rs:266-273), not plugin build. `SimRng::fork` requires a compile-time constant label (rng.rs:33-35): use `b"influence-op"`, `b"election"`, `b"coup"` and draw in BTreeMap order — never fork per country with a variable label. Cadence: `clock.new_month` (lib.rs:175-181) and tick stamps, never tick % N; elections must be dated from `GameDate` (1952 is a leap year — the CLAUDE.md test-cadence rule). Politics ordering is a chain (lib.rs:137-152): put `influence::update_influence` LAST in the chain (after `intel::update_espionage`) so ops see this month's network strength, and rely on the atomic `set_position` helper so basing/patron reads earlier in the same tick are never stale. Events apply in definition order (events.rs:439), so two same-tick shoves resolve deterministically.

findings.title: Two code paths bypass the 'no direct CountryDef reads' rule; pillar 2 needs a regime-openness notion distinct from alignment so one of them can stay
findings.detail: `Intel::ci_permille` reads `data.countries[c].alignment` directly to pick the counterintel floor (intel.rs:189-199; `CI_FLOOR_CLOSED = 300` for EasternBloc). world-timeline.md documents this as deliberate ('CI regime floors and economic-system seeding deliberately stay on the 1950 baseline (regime character, not current alignment)'), and planning.rs:205 seeds Planned/Market from static alignment for the same reason. But the defector roll reads static `c.stability` (intel.rs:603-607) while `Military::stability_of` (military.rs:380-385) is the dynamic accessor — an undocumented miss that AdjustStability events silently do not affect. Consequence for pillar 2: 'openness' (closed police state vs open society) must be its own per-country property (v1: derived from `Economies.system` Planned => closed, plus an explicit `closed` flag for regimes like Franco's Spain), used for (1) CI floors, (2) whether BackElection is even offered (no elections in closed regimes; coups instead), (3) propaganda effectiveness (open societies are easier to pull, harder to lock). Op difficulty should read the dynamic position and stability; regime character should not flip just because Cuba's position crossed a band edge in 1961. Fix the defector read as a one-line drive-by.

findings.title: The presentation surfaces are pre-built: a map-mode enum, a newspaper section registry with a reserved influence page, a panel template, and the wire
findings.detail: `MapMode` (map.rs:35) has six modes with a keyboard cycle (map.rs:786-791), button row (map.rs:516-554) and per-mode change detection (map.rs:952-956); an `Influence` mode is one enum arm plus a color fn (diverging red/blue by position, hatched when locked, outlined while contested). The paper (paper_ui.rs) already computes births from the Independence effect (paper_ui.rs:232-250) and has three rails (:348, :442, :523); newspaper.md reserves 'influence standings' and 'THE COLONIAL QUESTION (decolonization tracker)' as planned sections. intel_ui.rs:38-67 is the panel scaffold (toggle key + UGS_PANEL env boot + refresh + buttons enum) and its `grade()` (intel_ui.rs:69-76) is the house style for banding. Wire notices go through `FiredEvents.notices` (events.rs:49-51) and pull decisions through `FiredEvents.dynamic` (`DynamicChoice`, events.rs:24-35, used by the spy-trial at intel.rs:575-588) — the coup aftermath and election-result arcs should be DynamicChoices, which already route through the logged `ResolveEvent` command (command.rs:783-800). Foreign positions must render through the political-domain penetration band (Domain::Political, intel.rs:93) at 2 significant figures per the epistemics house rule.

findings.title: Aid has ready-made sinks and sources: GrantIndustry/GrantStock effects, distribute_proportional, the construction pool and military_stock
findings.detail: Scripted aid already exists as effects: `GrantIndustry { centi }` lands via `construction::distribute_proportional` (events.rs:225-227; construction.rs:583-620) and `GrantStock` adds to `military_stock` (events.rs:186-190; planning.rs:87). The player's spendable pools are `Construction.pool` (centi, capped at `POOL_CAP_CENTI = 4000`, construction.rs:26, 164) and `IndustryState.military_stock` (planning.rs:87). An `Aid` verb is therefore a command that moves centi from the sponsor's pool (or stock) to the recipient via the same helpers, plus a position nudge scaled by recipient size (a 300-centi grant moves Dahomey more than India) and a legitimacy credit to the sponsor. This makes aid a real guns-vs-butter trade against the player's own projects (pillar 4), which the sketch calls 'slow, safe, expensive'. Historical scale for tuning: Marshall Plan ~$13.3bn 1948-52 (about 5% of one year's US GDP); Soviet Aswan High Dam credit 1958 (~$100m first tranche); the CIA's 1948 Italian election effort is usually put at $1-2m — three orders of magnitude cheaper than aid, which is exactly the cost/risk asymmetry the verbs need.

findings.detail: `FLASHPOINTS` (crisis.rs:64-92) fix initiator/target as string tags (SOV->USA Berlin, PRC->USA Taiwan, SOV->TUR Straits). Once Turkey's position is live, the straits crisis should spawn only while TUR is Western or non-aligned and its target should be TUR's patron via `patrons_of`; a country the player has flipped should stop generating crises against its old patron. Deferred for v1 but worth noting because it is the concrete answer to 'what decision does a flipped alignment change' for pillar 1.
