mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Influence.position: one i16 West/East axis per country (-1000..+1000) with a derived three-band bloc, a lock timer, and a contested window; scripted SetAlignment becomes a band-edge shove
mechanics_recommendations.why: It keeps every existing alignment consumer untouched (they read the projected band via Military::alignment_of), gives the corpus's 29 SetAlignment uses a reversible meaning, and lets the acid test keep passing (Cuba lands in the Eastern band and stays there unless someone spends to pull it back). Commitment depth (sympathetic / aligned / treaty / satellite) is NOT a second state variable: it is |position| band plus `locked_until` — treaties and satellite status are locks set by events (Warsaw Pact, NATO accession) and settlement clauses, which is what makes Yugoslavia-1948 style drift possible only after a lock expires or is broken by an uprising event. Non-Aligned in v1 is the 0-band with passive gravity (uncontested positions decay toward 0 by NEUTRAL_DRIFT/month), i.e. a third attractor as a force, not an agent; Bandung 1955 and the 1961 Belgrade conference become events that widen the gravity and grant legitimacy to non-aligned states.
mechanics_recommendations.how: New `crates/ugs-sim/src/influence.rs`: `Influence { position: BTreeMap<CountryTag,i16>, locked_until: BTreeMap<CountryTag,u64>, contested_until: BTreeMap<CountryTag,u64>, ... }` with `tuning::{BAND_GATE=300, LOCK_GATE=700, NEWBORN_SEED=150, NEUTRAL_DRIFT=5, SHOVE_MARGIN=100}` and one mutation helper `set_position(&mut self, military: &mut Military, tag, value)` that also writes `military.alignments`. events.rs:210-218 calls the helper with band-edge semantics; new effects `ShiftAlignment{country,delta}` and `LockAlignment{country,months}` in ugs-data (validated like lib.rs:565-571; superpower tags rejected). Player reads it as the Influence map mode (diverging colour, hatch = locked, outline = contested) and as a verdict line per country: 'EGYPT: CONTESTED, LEANING EAST (est.), MOSCOW ACTIVE, NO TREATY'. Decision it changes: where to spend this month and whether a coup is even worth it (locked = no).

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Four verbs with disjoint currencies, timescales and exposure: Aid (pool/stock, overt, slow, safe), Presence (standing posture 0-3, overt, monthly pull, no risk), Back Election (one-shot, open regimes only, election window only, covert via the intel network), Sponsor Coup (one-shot, low-stability targets only, covert, fast flip, tension + deniability + legitimacy on exposure)
mechanics_recommendations.why: The sketch lists five tools by cost/risk but does not separate them by currency; if they all cost the same 'influence points' the player only ever picks the best rate, which is Twilight Struggle's known problem when coups are cheap (TS solves it by charging DEFCON — coups are exactly what an escalation game must price in tension). Aid competes with the player's own projects (construction pool, construction.rs:164), Presence competes with nothing but is capped in count (decision budget), Election/Coup spend the collection network the player also needs for intel (the OSO/OPC fratricide already modelled at intel.rs:439-444) plus deniability and, when blown, legitimacy. Each verb therefore changes a different existing decision: Aid vs build; Presence vs which 4-6 countries you care about; covert ops vs whether you can afford to lose your Iran network. Historical asymmetry to tune against: Marshall aid ~$13bn; TPAJAX (Iran 1953) and PBSUCCESS (Guatemala 1954) each low-single-digit $m; the 1948 Italian election ~$1-2m.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Commands in command.rs (player-gated like :823-837): `SetInfluencePresence{target, level:u8}` (cap PRESENCE_SLOTS=6 active per sponsor, like ZONE_CAP=3 at construction.rs:50), `SendAid{target, centi}` (moves pool centi via construction::distribute_proportional, nudge = centi * AID_PER_CENTI / recipient_pop_weight, sponsor legitimacy +1 per 300 centi), `LaunchInfluenceOp{target, kind: BackElection|SponsorCoup}` resolved in influence.rs using intel network strength (OP_MIN_STRENGTH/OP_STRENGTH_COST, intel.rs:51-53) and a shared `Intel::blow()` helper factored out of intel.rs:499-514. Coup: requires stability_of < COUP_STABILITY_GATE (50) and not locked; success => position to sponsor's band edge, stability -25, `AdjustStability`-style notice, then a DynamicChoice for the sponsor (recognise junta / stay quiet); blown => +BLOWN_TENSION (40, intel.rs:60), deniability -20, legitimacy -10, position -100 the other way (backfire), and a 'COVERT ACTION EXPOSED' notice usable as crisis pretext. Election: only offered by a pull event 'ELECTION IN {X}, {DATE}' created from a per-country `election_every_months`/anchor in data for open regimes; the op adds a one-time +/-ELECTION_SWING and the result is printed in the paper. Presentation: outcome ladders with PROBABLE/POSSIBLE/UNLIKELY words (espionage house rule), never percentages.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Bloc-leader monthly influence allocator: deterministic, published, attributed; plus two passive drifts (neutral gravity and a systems-competition pull from the living-standard differential)
mechanics_recommendations.why: AI participation with essentially zero AI code is the codebase's proven pattern (planning.rs:337-378 allocator; economic-agency.md 'zero new AI code'). Publishing the priority formula is what makes rival spend legible and counterable ('why is Moscow in Ghana?') — the same reason the market allocator records attribution. The SoL-differential drift is the cheapest honest hook for pillar 4: a country drifts a few points per month toward the bloc whose leader has the higher LivingStandards (demography.rs:84-86), so winning the economic race slowly paints the map even with no spending — the Khrushchev 'we will bury you' wager made mechanical.
mechanics_recommendations.how: In `update_influence` on `clock.new_month`: snapshot `position` (last month's values) then for each sponsor in fixed order [USA, SOV] (skip if player, pattern settlement.rs:1182): budget = actual_centi / INFLUENCE_BUDGET_DIVISOR; candidates = countries with |pos| < LOCK_GATE, not locked, not self; score = pop_weight(demo by current holder) * (1000 - |pos|) / 1000 * (contested ? 2 : 1) * (rival attributed here last month ? 2 : 1); take top INFLUENCE_AI_SLOTS (6) by score (tie-break tag order), split budget by largest remainder (planning.rs:363-375), apply nudge = share * NUDGE_PER_CENTI, record `attribution[(sponsor,target)] = share`. Drift: if nobody attributed a target this month, pos moves NEUTRAL_DRIFT toward 0; every month pos moves SOL_DRIFT * sign(SoL_USA - SoL_SOV) (clamped, never crossing a lock). Player reads it in the paper's INFLUENCE STANDINGS ('MOSCOW'S CHEQUEBOOK: INDONESIA, EGYPT, GHANA — WASHINGTON'S: ITALY, IRAN, JAPAN') and in the panel's per-country line; the decision it changes is where to counter-spend. Perf: O(sponsors x countries) per month, no pairwise table (avoid the O(n^2) trap intel.rs:141-147 documents).

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Decolonization as a contest: newborns seed contested, chains branch on the outcome via a new AlignmentBand trigger, and the paper gets THE COLONIAL QUESTION page
mechanics_recommendations.why: 37 new states already exist as data and 24 African independence events fire on schedule, but their alignment is a birth attribute nobody can influence. Making the Independence effect seed a contested position (inside the neutral band, leaning toward the data baseline) and opening a 36-month window with doubled effectiveness turns each birth into the 'renewable strategic frontier' the sketch promises. A trigger that reads the band lets content authors write consequence chains that depend on who won (Guinea courts Moscow only if Guinea is Eastern-leaning; the Congo crisis's Moscow branch only if Lumumba's government leans East), which is the one thing OptionChosen chains cannot express because the player's opponent, not the player, decided.
mechanics_recommendations.how: events.rs:228-297 Independence: after manpower seeding, `influence.set_position(military, country, baseline_pole * NEWBORN_SEED)` and `contested_until = tick + CONTEST_MONTHS*30*24`; the notice already says both blocs know it. ugs-data: `EventTrigger::AlignmentBand { country, band: String }` (validated against the three names), evaluated in `trigger_met` (events.rs:311-368). Content pass: convert ghana-pan-african-course options from SetAlignment to ShiftAlignment(+/-250) so Nkrumah's choice is a strong lean, not a lock; add AlignmentBand-gated variants for guinea-courts-moscow and congo-crisis-moscow. paper_ui.rs: a section listing every country whose contested window is open with its verdict line and who is outspending whom; the 'A NATION IS BORN' number line (paper_ui.rs:~480) links to it. Player decision changed: whether to pre-position presence in a colony's parent-region before the scheduled date the paper foreshadows ('GOLD COAST INDEPENDENCE SET FOR MARCH' from a Date trigger 12 months out).

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Give settlement outcomes and occupation teeth in the position: ClientState and Neutralization clauses write position and lock; released zones carry their popular alignment into the country position; crushing an uprising is priced in legitimacy and a lock
mechanics_recommendations.why: This is where pillars 1-2 join up: wars end in outcome objects (war-termination.md) that today only log. It also answers the sketch's 'domestic mirror' cheaply — satellites drift toward 0 when unlocked (Yugoslavia 1948 is a starting fact: YUG begins NonAligned-planned, planning.rs:205), a scripted uprising (hungary-uprising already in the corpus) offers 'CRUSH IT' = re-lock + legitimacy -15 + tension +40 vs 'LET IT GO' = unlock + ShiftAlignment toward 0, and allied democracies drift by SoL and by elections. World opinion is the existing legitimacy ledger, so no new currency.
mechanics_recommendations.how: settlement.rs:970-975 ClientState => set_position(state, patron band edge) + lock TRUCE_MONTHS; :987 Neutralization => set_position(state, 0) + lock; `evaluate` (settlement.rs:602+) adds a ledger term 'ORBIT: STATE'S POPULATION LEANS AWAY (-N)' from position; zone monthly drift (settlement.rs:1345-1352) also nudges the ORIGINAL owner's country position by drift/4 when policy is ClientAdministration; on Restore/treaty end, position += zone.alignment / 10 toward the holder's pole. Content: hungary-uprising options gain LockAlignment / ShiftAlignment and GrantLegitimacy deltas. Player reads it on the existing occupation card (war_ui.rs:2198-2225 already explains 'Alignment = whether the population accepts you') and in the treaty ledger; decision changed: which clause to pay for, and whether to hold a satellite by force.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Presentation slice: Influence map mode, one panel with verbs, one newspaper page, foreign positions seen through political penetration
mechanics_recommendations.why: House rules from both prior research passes: no panel without a verb; verdict sentences not tables; monthly date-stamped still display; what you see is what you believe. Espionage v1's political-domain penetration exists precisely so a second pillar can consume it — the player's read of Egypt's position should have a band width derived from `Intel::knowledge(me, EGY, Domain::Political)` exactly like war-UI fuzz widths.
mechanics_recommendations.how: map.rs:35 `MapMode::Influence` + colour fn (position -> diverging palette; unknown-band widening by penetration; locked hatch; contested outline) + cycle/button entries (:516-554, :786-791) + change detection on the Influence resource (:952-956). New `crates/ugs-app/src/influence_ui.rs` cloned from intel_ui.rs:38-100 (key `L`, `UGS_PANEL=influence`): rows = the player's presence slots + contested newborns + any country with an open pull event; each row = verdict sentence + buttons (Presence 0-3, Aid 300/600, Election when window open, Coup when eligible) — no row without a verb. paper_ui.rs: INFLUENCE STANDINGS in the right rail (bloc totals by population at 2 sig figs, this month's attributed spends, elections held) and THE COLONIAL QUESTION. Everything renders from `Influence` + `Intel` + `FiredEvents`; no UI-side sim state beyond the month snapshot pattern paper_ui already uses.

pitfalls: Whack-a-mole over 226 countries. If presence/aid can target anyone at any time the pillar becomes Vic3's 50-state queue. Enforce the decision budget structurally: PRESENCE_SLOTS cap (6) like ZONE_CAP, covert ops only via pull events (elections, contested windows, uprisings) or against countries with a funded network, and the AI allocator limited to the same slot count so rival activity is a readable list of six names, never a heat map of noise.

Two sources of truth for bloc. If any code path writes `military.alignments` without going through `Influence::set_position` (or vice versa), basing/patron reads and the influence map disagree silently. Route ALL writes through the one helper (events.rs:217 is the only current writer besides tests), add a monthly invariant assertion in a test (projected band == band(position) for every country after 20 hands-off years), and grep-review like world-timeline.md already mandates for CountryDef reads.

Allocator order dependence. If USA's allocator reads positions that SOV's allocator already moved this month (or the reverse), the result depends on iteration order and on whether the player is USA or SOV. Snapshot positions and attribution at month start; both sponsors read the snapshot and write into a delta map applied afterwards in BTreeMap order.

Coups as the dominant strategy. Twilight Struggle's design proves coups must spend escalation headroom (DEFCON) or players coup every turn. Gate coups on stability (< 50), on network strength (existing OP_MIN_STRENGTH), price them in tension even on success (a junta is a headline), and let them lock the target for the rival's counter-coup only briefly so the tug-of-war continues.

Scripted shoves that fight the player every month. If the corpus keeps hard SetAlignment semantics while the player spends to hold a country, the timeline reverts the player's work on a date. Band-edge shove semantics (no-op if already in band, minimal move otherwise) plus content review converting the reversible choices to ShiftAlignment keep both the acid test and the player's agency.

Cadence and RNG violations. Elections 'every 4 years' as tick modulo, per-country rng forks with variable labels, or floats for drift will all break replay. Use GameDate anchors (test the 1952 leap year and the 1950-01-01 start), constant fork labels drawn in BTreeMap order, and integer i16/u32 math like OccupationZone.alignment.

Forgetting the three registries and the digest gap. A new resource missing from lib.rs init, savegame.rs reset, or the savegame digest passes tests while replay silently diverges; the digest already omits Intel/Crises/Deterrence/Nuclear — add Influence and Intel at minimum.

Raw numbers leaking to the player. '+37 influence' and '62%' violate both prior readups. Show bands (CONTESTED / LEANING WEST / ALIGNED WEST / TREATY / SATELLITE), estimate language, and monthly date-stamped standings; hide the i16 entirely.

Superpower self-modification. Content or ops shifting USA/SOV (or a future PRC pole) breaks patrons_of and the allocator. Reject at load (ugs-data validation, like the unknown-alignment check at lib.rs:565-571) and in the command handlers.
analysts.first_hour_test: Boot as USA (UGS_NATION=USA, Jan 1 1950). Minute one: press the Influence map-mode button and read the world at a glance — the blue/red diverging map with hatched satellites (Warsaw-bloc locked), outlined contested states (Iran, Egypt, Italy, Indonesia, Guatemala — seeded from 1950 data as leaning but unlocked), and Korea/Japan/Philippines drawn as they are today via the unchanged basing rules. Open the Influence panel (L): at most six rows, each a verdict sentence with buttons — no row without a verb. The player sets Presence 2 on Iran and Italy and sends one 300-centi aid tranche to Egypt, visibly draining the construction pool in the econ panel (the guns-vs-butter trade is felt immediately). Advance to Feb 1: the paper's INFLUENCE STANDINGS prints Moscow's attributed spend ('MOSCOW'S CHEQUEBOOK: INDONESIA, EGYPT, IRAN') and the bloc-by-population totals at 2 significant figures; Egypt's line reads 'CONTESTED, LEANING EAST (EST.)' with a wider band than Italy's because political penetration on Egypt is embassy-only. March-April: one pull event arrives ('ELECTION IN ITALY SET FOR ...' or a contested-window notice), offering an outcome ladder in PROBABLE/POSSIBLE language, never a percentage; the player either acts or ignores it and nothing nags. By May the Iran row has changed band to 'LEANING WEST' as a result of the player's presence — the first alignment the player, not the script, moved. June 25: the Korean invasion fires unchanged; KOR/PRK/JAP basing and patrons behave exactly as before (regression: the_korean_war_runs_its_historical_arc and player_can_stand_aside pass). Acceptance: (1) map readable in under ten seconds, (2) no more than three pillar-2 decisions presented in the first six months, (3) one attributed rival spend line in the February paper, (4) one player-caused band change before June, (5) determinism: two hands-off runs and a save/replay with the three influence commands produce identical digests including Influence and Intel, (6) the_world_turns_to_1970 still passes with Cuba Eastern by 1965 and at least a dozen region-owning new states — now with non-baseline positions for some of them.

objections.target: systems-integration — 'Bloc-leader monthly influence allocator ... plus two passive drifts (neutral gravity and a systems-competition pull from the living-standard differential)'
objections.objection: The SoL-differential drift is a guaranteed ahistorical snowball. US living standards exceed Soviet ones for the entire 1950-1970 window, so every unlocked country drifts West every month for free, forever. Combined with the same analyst's uncapped `SendAid{target, centi}` (any country, any month, paid from a 4000-centi pool the US fills faster), the West paints the unlocked world by 1958 without a single interesting decision. The USSR player gets a game of bailing water. The fix the analyst offers (clamp, never crossing a lock) does not touch the sign problem.

objections.target: systems-integration — 'Four verbs with disjoint currencies' (SendAid) and board-game-contest-model — 'Turn-to-real-time translation: ~1.5-2 ops/month'
objections.objection: Two of the seven analysts reopen the bank. `SendAid` is a per-country, per-month cash verb with no slot — exactly the HoI4-PP/Superpower-2 pattern every other analyst lists as pitfall #1. And 1.5-2 ops/month is 18-24 ops/year against a TS baseline of ~17 ops per 4-year turn: five times TS density, so the 'coup every month' problem arrives by 1951 (history: nine major coup attempts in twenty years). Whatever the synthesis picks, aid must live in a slot and campaign-total ops must be anchored to history, not to a monthly budget that feels generous in a real-time UI.

objections.target: systems-integration — 'The AI precedent is a published deterministic allocator, not a planner'; board-game-contest-model — 'Region scoring ... doubles as the AI's utility function'
objections.objection: The AI opponent is a chequebook, not a rival. In every proposal the rival AI only places pips/aid via an allocator; coups, election pushes, crackdowns and withdrawals are player-gated commands (command.rs). So the player owns every fast verb and the AI owns only the slow one — a punching bag. Worse, the allocator's 'rival active here last month x2' and 'contested x2' multipliers make Moscow a dog that chases the player's ball: spend one slot in Iran to bait Soviet aid there, coup Guatemala unopposed. The board-game analyst's own evidence (COIN bot flowcharts) is ranked predicates over ALL verbs including coups; nobody wrote that flowchart.

objections.target: genre-influence-mechanics 'Three named factions per country'; domestic-mirror-and-bloc-discipline 'Three-seat country politics'; cold-war-influence-historian 'Faction ledger'; decolonization-contest 'Faction leans as the coup and drift surface'
objections.objection: Four analysts converge on 'three factions' and then each ships a different one: Government/Army/Street with grip pips; GOVERNMENT/STREET/GUNS plus depth plus a regime valve; ARMY/GOVERNMENT/STREET plus a LEADER bond plus army patron tag; government/army/party lean plus per-region street lean plus regime type plus power base plus inertia. That is 678 to 1,100+ drifting integers with uniform monthly rules the player never touches — a drift simulator with a BLOC STANDINGS page that lists RESTIVE/VOLATILE rows across 226 countries and implicitly asks 'so what are you going to do about it?' for each. Nobody shows that three fuzzed seats read through political-penetration brackets actually change a decision a single signed axis plus a stability number would not. The convergence is on the word 'three', not on a design.

objections.target: cold-war-influence-historian — 'Windows as the only moments the government line moves'; decolonization-contest — 'The Independence Opening'
objections.objection: 'Alignment moves only at windows' plus a real-time hourly clock is dead air. At speed 3 a month is ~a minute; if the government line can only change on ~10 election dates a year plus scheduled independences, the player sets a slot and waits — the Stellaris-envoy set-and-forget texture the legibility analyst already condemns. The historian's own decision density (2-4 windows/month 'in 1958-62') is a 1958 number; in 1950-54 the corpus has a handful of elections and zero independences, so the tutorial half-decade is a wait simulator precisely where the vision doc wants the player to learn the pillar.

objections.target: cold-war-influence-historian — 'Bids: the aid verb as a named, priced offer ... rival bids visible through political intel'
objections.objection: The auction needs an auctioneer nobody builds. Nasser showing the Soviet offer to Dulles requires a recipient AI that solicits, compares and leaks bids; the analyst's own pitfall says 'Non-Aligned as a passive middle' is fatal, yet the mechanic as specified reduces to 'aid with an announcement bonus and a delivery clock' because the recipient's only behaviour is accept. Without a recipient decision rule (which bid wins, when does it leak, when does it expel advisers) the auction is a slower aid slider, and the 'withdrawal as crisis pretext' branch is a button the AI never presses against the player.

objections.target: board-game-contest-model — 'Non-Aligned ... is an emergent equilibrium plus a saturation rule'; systems-integration — 'Non-Aligned in v1 is the 0-band with passive gravity'
objections.objection: A 'field' is something the player watches, not plays. Neutral gravity (NEUTRAL_DRIFT toward 0 wherever nobody spent) and saturation backlash are pure decay rules: the only verb they create is 'spend more to fight the decay', which is the maintenance loop the espionage house rules ban. Meanwhile the field answers the sketch's open question by dodging it — Nehru, Nasser and Tito never do anything. And the decay-plus-uncapped-aid combination is the Vic2 'bank hits 100, click' cadence with the numbers hidden.

objections.target: domestic-mirror-and-bloc-discipline — 'World-opinion payout as seat deltas in other countries, not a global scalar'
objections.objection: The bill for Hungary lands where it cannot hurt. Crushing Budapest shifts the UK and Italian STREET seats a hair away from Moscow — but the USSR player was never going to win a British election, so the payout is invisible and the correct play is always crush (the analyst's own pitfall). The attention-scaling rule makes it worse: crush during a war or Brink and the cost halves, so the optimal Soviet play is to time crackdowns to crises, which is cute once and a degenerate loop thereafter. The only part with teeth is the never-decaying `crushed_count` — keep that, but the rival-street cost needs to hit something the crusher actually competes for (battleground standings, NAM prestige, the next checkpoint score) or it is decoration.

objections.target: decolonization-contest — 'The UN General Assembly session as the annual scoring surface' and 'Bids as five typed verbs ... plus the metropole as a separate AI with a reversal right'
objections.objection: Scope explosion dressed as a v1 slice. A UNGA session with 3-5 data-driven resolutions per year, issue-tagged votes computed per member, a 90-day vote-buying window, a metropole AI with residual weight and a 48-hour reversal decision, five typed bid verbs, regime type, power base, wave ids, per-region street lean, and cadre bids with a 5-10 year payout — none of which the player can feel in the first hour, all of which need sourced content for 226 countries. The UNGA tally is also tautological as a score: it is computed from the alignment the standings page already shows, so the player watches a second display of the same number. Cut to: Independence seeds a contested window; a chain trigger reads the band.

objections.target: board-game-contest-model — 'Realignment is the adjacency mechanic ... a contiguity engine' and 'Reach rule and superpower adjacency'
objections.objection: Adjacency bonuses without cards are a regional snowball generator. TS balances +1-per-adjacent-controlled with a fixed card hand and DEFCON; in a sim with a monthly budget the bloc that dominates a region strips the rival's remnants for near-free and the map paints contiguously by 1958. The analyst names this in 'Snowball through adjacency' and then recommends both realignment rolls and reach anyway, relying on saturation backlash and NAM decay (both passive) to hold it back. Nothing in the set is a comeback mechanic for the losing bloc.

objections.target: legibility-and-decision-budget — 'The monthly heartbeat: ... a briefing card with one recommendation'
objections.objection: A correct recommendation derived from visible data plays the game for the player ('RECOMMEND: ELECTION PUSH IN TURKEY'); an incorrect one is noise. Either way it is the opposite of the pillar's promise that reading the world is the skill. The same analyst's designated ~12-15 battlegrounds 'per era' also leak the script: if Angola is a battleground marker in 1965 regardless of what the player did, the board is telling the player what the timeline knows.

objections.target: board-game-contest-model — 'The coup formula d6 + ops - 2*stability defines a hard frontier'; genre-influence-mechanics — 'Stability as the price of a flip'
objections.objection: With 73 of 86 sovereigns at stability 60 (stab_ts = 3), the TS frontier makes every country the same coin flip on day one; the analyst notes the flat table and then defers the historian pass to 'must ship with the mechanic', which in practice means the first playable build has no difficulty surface. And the escalation price is symmetric across the map at Wary: at start tension is 30 with all regions open, so the cheapest verb in the game is a coup, everywhere, until Korea. Coups also have a mirror only the player can pull (see the AI objection).

objections.target: legibility-and-decision-budget — 'Epistemic texture: true alignment vs the embassy estimate'
objections.objection: Fog is applied only where the player is not acting: own-bloc members and any country with a standing program get near-exact reads, so the bracket exists exactly on the rows the player does not care about. At LIMITED coverage the bracket is +/-4 notches on a 21-notch axis while the band gate sits at +/-300/1000, so the player cannot distinguish CONTESTED from LEANING — the decision the display is supposed to change becomes a guess. That is texture, not a decision input; fine as flavor, but do not claim it as the pillar's differentiator.

objections.target: domestic-mirror-and-bloc-discipline — 'Scheduled election valve with a real calendar'; legibility-and-decision-budget — 'historical decision cadence ... election dates'
objections.objection: ~40 democracies on real cycles over 20 years is 200+ dated events the player mostly has no stake in, each printing a wire line and rolling a die the player watches (Belgium, June 1950). The espionage rule 'every output changes a decision' fails for the majority of those lines; the heartbeat cap of 6 lines helps, but nobody says which elections are content and which are silent.

missing: A rival AI that uses the fast verbs. Every proposal gives the AI an aid allocator and gives the player coups, election pushes, withdrawals and crackdowns. The synthesis needs a ranked-predicate bot (COIN-style) over the full verb set, or the contest is one-sided; and it needs the bot to be legible so the player can read 'why Moscow is in Ghana' without it being exploitable bait.

One state model. The set contains four incompatible substrates (two influence piles; signed i16 + lock + contested window; three seats + depth + valve; four leans + regime type + power base + inertia). Nobody reconciles them, and the systems-integration proposal (the only one grounded in the code) is the thinnest. The synthesis must pick one and say what is deferred to v1.5.

What alignment buys. Beyond basing (already via alignment_of) and a checkpoint score, nothing says what losing Italy or winning Egypt costs or yields in the other three pillars — trade access, intel embassy floors, crisis flashpoint participants, proxy-war patronage. Systems-integration flags crisis flashpoints and defers it. Without stakes, standings are a scoreboard the player watches.

A comeback mechanic for the losing bloc. TS has the card hand and scoring-card timing; nothing here gives the side behind on standings a cheaper verb, a bigger NAM pull, or a world-opinion windfall. Every proposed brake (saturation, neutral gravity, hysteresis) is passive.

Pacing between windows in a real-time hourly sim. What does the pillar give the player to do in Feb-May 1950, and in 1951-54 before Bandung and the decolonization wave? Nobody tests 'is there a decision this month' across the dead years; all first-hour tests stop at Korea.

A cross-pillar decision budget. Economy claims 2-4/month, espionage its own, war termination its own, and the influence proposals add 1-2 plus 3-6 heartbeat lines plus embassy-report cards plus election popups. Nobody sums them; the legibility analyst's 'near 6/month total' is asserted, not shown.

A hands-off baseline. With contest, drift and allocator on and no player, does the AI-vs-AI world still land roughly historical (Cuba East by 1962, Egypt NAM, Eastern Europe held, Africa mixed) at 1970? Systems-integration mentions the_world_turns_to_1970 but nobody defines the tolerance or the tuning loop to hit it.

A first-hour test as a minor. All seven tests play the USA (one adds a USSR mirror). Nobody asks what India, Yugoslavia, France or Egypt does in this pillar, though several proposals (NAM prestige, metropole bidder, the auction) only exist if a non-superpower can act.

Tuning numbers in one table. First values are scattered (BAND_GATE 300, PRESENCE_SLOTS 6, 3 slots, 1.5-2 ops/month, +150 tension per battleground coup, 24- or 36-month newborn windows). The synthesis needs one `tuning` table with the historical anchor for each number and the acid test each number must keep passing.
keep: systems-integration 'Influence.position: one i16 axis per country with a derived three-band bloc' — a fine position behind the single `Military::alignment_of` accessor, written only through one atomic helper; `SetAlignment` becomes a band-edge shove with new `ShiftAlignment`/`LockAlignment` effects so the 29 scripted decrees stop overruling the player. This is the integration everyone else assumes and nobody else specified.

Slot-capped standing programs, never a bank (genre 'Influence programs as a capped portfolio'; legibility 'Capped commitment slots'): fixed per rank, no upkeep, auto-suspend on expulsion so orphans are impossible, and 'dropping one is the decision'. Aid must live inside this, not beside it.

Coups gated on visible local facts and priced in politics (historian 'Covert flip operations'; board-game 'coup frontier'; legibility 'Kent-word outcome ladder'): army lean + stability as the printed frontier, network strength consumed via intel.rs, tension/deniability/legitimacy on the ladder, and a backfire branch that moves the target AGAINST the sponsor. The Kent legend printed once is the right honesty compromise.

Tension band gates regions in war-start order and battleground coups pay tension (board-game 'DEFCON coupling'): the one coupling that makes pillar 2 live inside pillar 1 with zero new resources, plus the content rule that nothing may force a coup at Brink.

Hysteresis and lock timers (genre 'commitment ladder'; systems-integration `locked_until`): treaty/satellite as locks set by events and settlement clauses, exit thresholds below entry thresholds, reversal cost rising with recency — the Terra Invicta/Vic2 lesson.

Regional Presence/Domination/Control standings with a sourced battleground set, rendered monthly as the reserved newspaper page and read by era checkpoints (board-game 'Region scoring'; genre 'INFLUENCE STANDINGS'): the scoreboard that makes 226 countries a triage list, provided battlegrounds do not leak the script.

Independence seeds a contested window instead of a fixed alignment; chains retarget to `ShiftAlignment`; an `AlignmentBand` trigger lets content branch on who won (systems-integration 'Decolonization as a contest'; decolonization 'Engine collision' finding): the minimal fix that turns 37 scripted births into contests.

Elections as scheduled valves with a date the player sees months ahead, and pre-date verbs as the only way to move a democracy's government (domestic-mirror 'Scheduled election valve') — for battleground democracies only, silent elsewhere.

Crush pays a never-decaying memory term and tolerate opens the rival's aid verb (domestic-mirror 'World-opinion payout'), with the caveat that the crush bill must hit something the crusher competes for.

Aid's effect lands at announcement and withdrawal, and withdrawal is a crisis pretext (historian 'Economic aid consolidated alignment'): cheap to model as a step plus a delivery clock; keep even if the full auction is deferred.
A sourced per-country stability pass to replace the flat 60 (board-game 'Flat stability' pitfall) shipping in the same commit as the coup verb.

Foreign positions rendered through political-domain penetration with AS-OF stamps and public/covert provenance (legibility 'Epistemic texture'; systems-integration) — as flavor and as a reason to fund networks, not as the pillar's core claim.

objections.target: systems-integration — 'Bloc-leader monthly influence allocator… plus two passive drifts (neutral gravity and a systems-competition pull from the living-standard differential)'
objections.objection: Fails the hands-off timeline test on two counts. (1) SoL drift: `compute_sol` (demography.rs:88-96) is 5 + 60*(industry per M pop) + 40*urban share; the USA's value dwarfs the USSR's for the entire 1950-70 run, so every unlocked country drifts West every month for twenty years. The hands-off 1965 then reads as a Western Third World — the opposite of the Soviet aid offensive, Bandung and Belgrade. (2) Neutral gravity (NEUTRAL_DRIFT toward 0 for any country the two 6-slot AI allocators did not touch this month) means ~100 countries at a Western/Eastern baseline decay to the NonAligned band within a year unless locked, and there is no lock table: CountryDef carries alignment/stability/industry/nuclear_power only (ugs-data lib.rs:68-82), no NATO/Rio/ANZUS/Warsaw membership. Japan (WesternBloc, stability 65) or the FRG sliding to NonAligned before June 1950 breaks `friendly_soil` basing (military.rs:540-574) that the Korean-War regression tests the same analyst cites depend on. Ship a sourced treaty/lock seed first or drop both drifts from v1.

objections.target: board-game-contest-model — 'Two influence piles per country with a stability-margin control test' and 'Reach rule and superpower adjacency'
objections.objection: The proposed 1950 seed is Twilight Struggle's 1945-era setup, and it contradicts the scenario data and basing rules on day one: Japan 'US 1' against stab 3 (from the flat 60/20) fails the margin test, so SCAP-occupied Japan (data: WesternBloc, stability 65, generated.ron:427-430) reads NonAligned on 1 Jan 1950 and loses its basing role for Korea; Cuba is NonAligned in the data (generated.ron:177), not the Western holding TS implies. The reach rule ('USSR land reach only until a 1960s navy event') is ahistorical for exactly the decade the pillar is about: the Czech arms deal to Egypt (Sept 1955), credits to Indonesia (1956), Guinea (1959), Ghana (1960) and Cuba (1960) were all non-contiguous. A hands-off run under that rule has Moscow unable to bid on any of its actual 1955-65 clients, which is the inverse of history.

objections.target: board-game-contest-model — 'Events the opponent must play… converting SetAlignment decrees into influence pushes' (and decolonization-contest 'Engine collision')
objections.objection: Cuba's Eastern alignment in the acid test comes from `cuba-turns-east` (OptionChosen us-embargo-decision option 0 + 179 days, SetAlignment). If that becomes '+4 East, -3 West' deltas while the US allocator counter-spends (Cuba scores maximally: contested, rival active) and neutral gravity pulls toward 0, `the_world_turns_to_1970`'s CUB == EasternBloc assertion (events.rs:1003-1008) becomes seed-dependent, and `chains_fire_on_schedule_and_flip_alignment` ('SetAlignment overrides the 1950 baseline', events.rs:876) breaks outright. systems-integration's band-edge shove semantics (no-op if already in band) keeps both tests; delta semantics do not. Separately, the 'historian pass on per-country stability replacing the flat 60' targets `countries/generated.ron`, which CLAUDE.md forbids hand-editing — it has to go into the nationgen/mapgen source table, and nobody says so.

objections.target: genre-influence-mechanics — 'Three named factions… Government disposition is pulled toward Street each cycle in democracies'; domestic-mirror-and-bloc-discipline — 'Scheduled election valve… GOVERNMENT moves toward STREET by a fraction'
objections.objection: A pull-toward-street rule produces a hands-off Western Europe history never showed. France's street was 25-28% PCF for a decade and Italy's 22-27% PCI rising every election, yet neither government moved because coalition formation was a majority-of-non-communists rule (the conventio ad excludendum the domestic-mirror analyst cites), not an average of leans. Averaging a 'DIVIDED' street into the government seat over four or five electoral cycles drifts FRA/ITA toward the NonAligned band by 1960 with no player action. Elections need a threshold/coalition resolution (the hostile pole governs only if its street share clears a majority or a stability-scaled gate), which also makes the +3-point election-interference calibration meaningful: three points matter only near a threshold.

objections.target: cold-war-influence-historian — 'Windows as the only moments the government line moves' and 'Faction ledger under the government line'
objections.objection: Historically right, but as specified it cannot run the era spine hands-off. Resolving each window 'from the resolving factions plus a seeded roll from b"windows"' makes Turkey 1950, Italy 1953, FRG 1953 and every 1960 birth stochastic per seed, and it needs seeded faction leans for 226+37 countries, an army-patron tag, and a sourced election calendar for ~40 democracies — none exist in the data and no analyst scopes the pass. The corpus's 29 SetAlignment events and 182 AdjustStability are already the windows; the coherent v1 is: scripted window outcomes stay the default when nobody spent (band-edge shove), and a roll happens only where a bloc has committed. Otherwise 'money outside a window is stored, not spent' also means months with zero feedback, violating the espionage rule that every output changes a decision.

objections.target: decolonization-contest — 'The Independence Opening', 'UN General Assembly session as the annual scoring surface', and the first-hour VIETNAM recognition race
objections.objection: There is no Vietnam to recognize in the first hour: VNN/VNS are born via independence.ron (Geneva 1954); DRV/State of Vietnam are not 1950 tags. 'Indonesia closing on UN admission' presumes a UN object that does not exist. The UNGA scoring surface needs a membership table (60→117), issue-tagged resolutions, and a vote model for 226 tags including colonies — a second scoring system on top of the newspaper standings page already reserved, and a v2-sized content pass. The 'metropole as a separate AI with a 48-hour reversal right' is a decision event, and AI countries resolve decisions with option 0 at the deadline (events.rs:403-458), so the metropole 'AI' is a scripted default; say so and author it as data. The per-state regime type and power base fields are good but again unsourced for 37 newborns and 86 sovereigns.

objections.target: genre-influence-mechanics 'Non-Aligned … overt coups shift every NAM member's Street', cold-war-influence-historian 'World opinion as a bounded global pool', domestic-mirror 'World-opinion payout as seat deltas', board-game '13 Days World Opinion modifier'
objections.objection: Four incompatible world-opinion models, and only systems-integration notices the game already has one: `Settlements.legitimacy` (settlement.rs:256/281), per country, written by `hungary-soviet-decision` (-15 SOV on CRUSH), `france-nato-exit` (-5 USA), Exploitation zones (-1/month), and spent as a hard gate on high-sovereignty treaty clauses (settlement.rs:745-748) and displayed in war_ui/paper_ui. The domestic-mirror claim that 'a global scalar changes no decision' is false on the record. Adding a bloc-signed pool or per-country seat payouts on top double-models it. Pick legitimacy as the world-opinion currency; if seat deltas are wanted later, derive them from a legitimacy delta, don't store a second ledger.

objections.target: board-game 'PROVEN-attributed coup banks a crisis pretext through the existing attribution machine'; historian 'PROVEN attribution flips the push negative'; legibility 'attribution moves UNATTRIBUTED → SUSPECTED → PROVEN by named objects'
objections.objection: The three-state attribution machine is designed in espionage.md §3 but not implemented: intel.rs:446-514 rolls a single `blown` boolean, applies the effect 'regardless of exposure', spends deniability, adds BLOWN_TENSION and emits a notice — no evidence objects, no SUSPECTED state, no pretext registration (crisis.rs has three hard-coded FLASHPOINTS and `spawn_ultimatum`, nothing pretext-driven). Every PROVEN-conditional branch in these recommendations is resting on absent code. Either the slice scopes the machine in (an espionage v1.5 item) or v1 coup/election ops branch on blown/not-blown only.

objections.target: genre 'Rival AI uses the same portfolio with an auto-allocator'; board-game 'AI bloc monthly pick = argmax marginal scoring gain'; historian 'AI-vs-AI contests resolve from the same ledger silently'
objections.objection: All three assume AI blocs can run coups and election ops through the espionage layer. They cannot: FundNetwork, SetCounterintel and LaunchOperation are player-gated (command.rs:824-837), no AI ever funds a network, and OP_MIN_STRENGTH = 40 means an unfunded AI network can never mount an op. So a hands-off 1953-65 has zero AI coups unless Iran/Guatemala/Iraq/Congo/Brazil/Indonesia stay scripted timeline events — which is fine and historically correct, but must be stated: v1 AI runs only overt verbs (aid/presence), coups are timeline events plus a player-only op. Otherwise 'zero new AI code' is false — an AI espionage policy is new AI.

objections.target: domestic-mirror-and-bloc-discipline — 'Three-seat country politics… `OccupationZone.alignment` is the STREET seat… should be promoted to a country-level field'; systems-integration 'one unit, one mental model'
objections.objection: `OccupationZone.alignment` is holder-relative ('popular disposition toward the holder', keyed (holder, original owner), settlement.rs:117-135, drifting by zone policy), not a West/East axis. The same value means opposite things under a Soviet and an American holder, and is undefined for a NonAligned holder. Promoting it to a bloc-axis STREET seat, or flowing it into a country position on zone release, is a frame conversion through the holder's bloc, not a shared unit. Also the drift rule scales by 'regime openness' via CI_FLOOR, which is read from static 1950 alignment (intel.rs:189-199) — there is no openness field, so Cuba after 1961 or Guinea after 1959 keep their 1950 openness forever.

objections.target: domestic-mirror-and-bloc-discipline — 'Asymmetric patron discipline verbs: … CRUSH: the client's territory becomes an occupation zone held by the patron'
objections.objection: Double-models the timeline and misuses the zone machinery. `hungary-soviet-decision` already scripts the crush (AdjustTension 50, AdjustStability -15, GrantLegitimacy -15 SOV/-15 HUN, spawned divisions) as a SOV decision. Occupation zones are derived each pass from the occupation overlay of provinces held by a belligerent that is not the owner, inside a war; a crush without a war state has no (holder, original owner) zone to key and would need a garrison/occupation-without-war concept that settlement::update does not have. The sketch's mirror is satisfiable with a lock + legitimacy + stability price on the existing event options (systems-integration's version), not a new occupation path.

objections.target: systems-integration 'AlignmentBand trigger', decolonization 'chains branch on the outcome', historian 'withdrawal banks a grievance the timeline's crisis triggers can read'
objections.objection: Only systems-integration proposes the actual missing piece: `EventTrigger` has Date / WarDaysElapsed / ProvincesLost / TensionAbove/Below / EventFired / OptionChosen (ugs-data lib.rs:182-217) — nothing reads alignment, stability, legitimacy or a grievance. Without a band/threshold trigger the timeline keeps firing `cuba-turns-east`, `guinea-courts-moscow`, `congo-*` chains regardless of who won the contest, which is a silent double-model in the other direction (the player flips Cuba West in 1960, the missile crisis arrives anyway). The historian's and decolonization analyst's chains-that-branch-on-outcome are unimplementable until that trigger exists; it should be in the v1 slice, and content review must retarget the ~10 chains that assume the historical outcome.

objections.target: genre 'commitment ladder Contested | Leaning | Aligned | Treaty | Satellite'; legibility 'depth saturation'; decolonization 'commitment depth'; systems-integration 'depth = |position| band plus locked_until'
objections.objection: Every ladder needs a 1950 seed of who is Treaty/Satellite (NATO 1949 twelve, Rio Pact, Cominform/Warsaw-to-be, Commonwealth defence ties, French Union), and none exists in data — CountryDef has no membership field and events grant NATO accession only for FRG/TUR-style scripted cases. Without that seed, hysteresis and locks apply to nobody in 1950 and the 'satellites cannot be realigned below control' floor is empty. This is a scenario-data pass through the generator pipeline (scenario-data skill), and it gates every proposal here.

objections.target: board-game 'Tension gating and pricing lifted from DEFCON'; domestic-mirror 'attention scaling… multiplied in Calm'
objections.objection: The tension meter is not DEFCON: it decays at 2 + value/250 tenths per day to ERA_FLOOR 150 (tension.rs:11-18, 92-93), so from the 300 start it reaches the Calm band in about seven weeks and, between event spikes (mostly +5..+20, tension corpus histogram), a hands-off run sits in Calm most of the time. 'Wary: all open' and 'Calm multiplies the crush penalty' are therefore effectively always-on, and 'three battleground coups push Wary into Crisis' assumes a baseline that the meter does not hold. Gate tables must be tuned against the actual hands-off tension trace, and the band arithmetic in intel.rs (`value/250` → 0-3) is the existing convention to reuse.

objections.target: legibility-and-decision-budget — 'What the codebase gives the slice for free' and 'Capped commitment slots… +1 at the Korea/NSC-68 funding step-change event'
objections.objection: `GreatProjectDef.payload Influence(i32)` does not exist; the variant is `Prestige { tension_relief: i32 }` (ugs-data lib.rs:412-413) with a comment 'influence later', and no `Influence` identifier appears anywhere in ugs-data/ugs-sim. synthesis.shape:
STATE. A new `crates/ugs-sim/src/influence.rs` resource `Influence` holds, per country in BTreeMaps: `position: i16` (-1000..+1000), `baseline: i16` (the 1950 seed the position decays toward, never past), `locked_until: Option<tick>`, `contested_until: Option<tick>`, `last_band_change: tick`, `army_patron: Option<Pole>` (a coup-gate flag only, no faction ledger), and `crushed_count: u8`. A `Standings` block (per-region Presence/Domination/Control, denied counts) is recomputed on `new_month`; a `Checkpoints` resource freezes it at 1955-01-01 and 1960-01-01 and is digest-folded. Positions seed from existing CountryDef alignment (+/-450 for an aligned baseline, +/-700 and locked for treaty/satellite per the new seed table, 0 for NonAligned), not from Twilight Struggle's 1945 board, so Japan and West Germany read Western with basing intact on day one. Bands: |pos| >= 300 enters WesternBloc/EasternBloc, |pos| < 150 leaves (hysteresis), |pos| >= 700 or a lock timer reads as Treaty/Satellite for display and for verb gating. Openness is its own per-country property (v1 derived from `Economies.system` Planned => closed, plus an explicit `closed` flag for Spain/Portugal-type regimes) and replaces the static-alignment CI floor read; it gates whether elections exist and halves Presence rates. The only passive motion in v1: program-bought lean decays at 5/month toward `baseline` when no program is active on the country (dropping a program is the price, running one is not upkeep); after the Bandung event, unlocked countries adjacent to a NAM champion pull 5/month toward 0. There is NO living-standard drift and NO gravity toward 0 for baseline positions: the skeptics' fatal objection (the West paints the unlocked world by 1958; ~100 countries decay to NonAligned before Korea) is resolved by deleting both rules from v1 and moving the systems-competition term to a checkpoint score line in v2. Reversal cost rises with recency: a country that changed band within the last 12 months moves at half rate back.

VERBS. Two price shapes. STANDING PROGRAMS (slots: USA/SOV 3 in 1950, +1 from a dated unlock event to be authored for the 1951 Mutual Security Act and the Nov 1955 Khrushchev-Bulganin tour; UK/FRA 2; other majors 1; minors 0), each = (target, kind, tier 1-3), persisting with zero upkeep, auto-suspending with a wire line if the target locks against the sponsor. AID PROGRAM: draws 300 centi/tier/month from the construction pool via `distribute_proportional` (a real guns-vs-butter trade against the player's own projects), lands an announcement step of +50 toward the sponsor on the month it starts, then flows +10/+20/+30 per month scaled by target size (small states x2, contested-window x2), and has a WITHDRAW command that refunds undelivered centi, shoves -100 the other way and adds +5.0 tension (Aswan, 19-26 July 1956). PRESENCE (radio + missions): near-free in centi, occupies a slot, +5/+10/+15 per month halved in closed regimes, unlocked for the US by the Campaign of Truth event (20 Apr 1950) and RFE (4 Jul 1950); Moscow starts with it. ACTIVE OPS (1 slot, 2 from 1955), routed through `intel.rs` with the existing OP_MIN_STRENGTH/OP_STRENGTH_COST/blown roll factored into a shared `Intel::blow()` helper: ELECTION PUSH, offered only by a pull event 6 months before a battleground democracy's sourced election date (UK 23 Feb 1950, Greece 5 Mar 1950, Turkey 14 May 1950, France Jun 1951, Italy 7 Jun 1953, FRG 6 Sep 1953, Chile 4 Sep 1964...), adds a bounded +/-60 to the election's seeded roll (`b\"elections\"`, Levin's 'about three points'), and if blown flips the push negative, spends deniability and debits legitimacy; SPONSOR COUP, offered only when `stability_of(target) < 50`, `army_patron` is the sponsor or None, the target is not locked, and the tension band is below the region's gate (Crisis closes Europe; Brink closes Europe, Asia and the Middle East; nothing may ever force a coup at Brink), prepared over 3 months with clean abort, resolved via `b\"coup\"` on a printed frontier ('STAB 38 - ARMY: US-EQUIPPED - NETWORK L2 - COUP: PROBABLE') and a five-rung ladder CLEAN FLIP / FLIP WITH EVIDENCE / QUIET FIZZLE / EXPOSED FAILURE / CIVIL WAR labelled with Kent words and one legend in the panel footer; success sets position to the sponsor's band edge (+/-350), stability -25, tension +15.0 in a battleground or +5.0 elsewhere, legitimacy -5, and a DynamicChoice (recognise the junta / stay quiet); exposure branches on the existing blown boolean only (the PROVEN three-state machine is not implemented and is the first deferred item): +40 tension, deniability -20, legitimacy -10, position -150 against the sponsor, 'COVERT ACTION EXPOSED' notice. Elections in battleground democracies resolve by a threshold rule, not a pull toward an average: the government's band changes only if the seeded roll plus programs plus pushes clears the hysteresis gate, so France and Italy hold Western through a decade of 25% communist votes exactly as history did. Ops density is anchored to history by structure, not budget: one op slot with 3-month prep caps a superpower at four coup attempts a year before tension gates bite (history: nine major attempts in twenty years), and network strength must be rebuilt between them.

SURFACES. (1) `MapMode::Influence`: diverging hue by position, saturation stepped by depth, hatch = locked, outline = contested window open, desaturated hatch = below LIMITED political coverage; battleground pips only for the sourced set plus open windows; colour-blind safe because depth and contest are also carried by saturation and markers. (2) One politics panel (`UGS_PANEL=influence`, cloned from intel_ui) whose default tab is the ~12-row BATTLEGROUNDS triage list (COUNTRY | POSITION band with estimate bracket | DEPTH | TREND + cause word | NEXT valve | OURS exact | THEIRS estimate or '?' | COVERAGE), chips MY BLOC / NEWBORN / CONTESTS <= 6 MO / ALL last, a COMMITMENTS tab showing n/cap, and a one-page political dossier per country in the region-dossier form: header (NationMeta, or 'PROVISIONAL GOVERNMENT' for the 37 newborns), axis strip with penetration-width bracket stamped AS OF month, a signed PRESSURES ledger of <= 6 named terms, NEXT block, verdict footer, verb buttons whose disabled state prints why. (3) The newspaper's INFLUENCE STANDINGS page (bloc totals by states/population/industry at 2 sig figs, per-region verdict words, top-5 movers with cause, both chequebooks, 'FOREIGN COMMITMENTS ARE ESTIMATES' footer) and THE COLONIAL QUESTION page (open windows, months remaining, believed lean). (4) Wire: <= 6 lines per month with a cause each; pull cards only for election windows, contested windows, coup eligibility and uprisings.

AI PARTICIPATION. One monthly allocator per bloc leader (USA, SOV; skip the player), budget = industry actual_centi / INFLUENCE_BUDGET_DIVISOR, candidates = unlocked countries with |pos| < 700, score = battleground weight (population by current holder) x (1000 - |pos|) x (contested window ? 2 : 1), top 3 by score with tag tie-break, largest-remainder split, attribution recorded and printed; both leaders read the month-start snapshot and write into a delta map applied in BTreeMap order. No 'rival active here' multiplier (it made Moscow a dog chasing the player's ball). AI blocs run no coups or election pushes in v1: Iran 1953, Guatemala 1954, Iraq 1958, Congo 1960 and Brazil 1964 remain timeline events with their SetAlignment effects converted to band-edge shoves, and the AI's covert layer is the first item in the return queue. AI democracies run the election valve; AI metropoles and newborns resolve decision events by the data default (option 0), authored as content, never described as AI.

DECOLONIZATION CONTEST. Independence (events.rs:228-297) seeds position = baseline_pole x 150 inside the NonAligned band, sets `contested_until` = birth + 24 months, doubles program rates and suspends hysteresis inside the window; the window closes at its date, on the first lock, or on a coup, and the close is a paper headline ('GHANA GOES NON-ALIGNED; HARD TO MOVE'). A data-declared lead notice per independence event ('GOLD COAST INDEPENDENCE SET FOR MARCH', sourced to when the date was actually announced, never the raw script date) lets a sponsor hold a Presence program on the parent territory up to 12 months early; the newborn inherits that program's accumulated lean at birth. The 1960 wave is bundled by a wave id so the paper prints one COLONIAL QUESTION table with ranked rows and the slot cap forces choosing two or three states, the way Moscow concentrated on Guinea/Ghana/Mali. The ~10 outcome-assuming chains are retargeted: ghana-pan-african-course options become ShiftAlignment(+/-250); guinea-courts-moscow, congo-crisis-moscow and cuba-turns-east gain AlignmentBand-gated variants so the missile crisis does not arrive in a Cuba the player flipped West; katanga-reintegrated shoves rather than sets.

DOMESTIC MIRROR. Same position, same dossier, same page: MY BLOC is a filter chip. Satellites are locked at seed; the existing uprising events (Berlin 1953, Poznan/Hungary 1956) gain option effects CRUSH = LockAlignment 60 months + GrantLegitimacy -15 + tension +50 + `crushed_count` += 1, versus TOLERATE = unlock + ShiftAlignment toward 0 + the existing five-satellite stability contagion + the rival's AID verb opens on that country. Crush is not modelled through occupation zones (they are derived from wars and holder-relative; the skeptic's objection stands). Allied battleground democracies run the election valve and can drop a depth rung (France 1966 style events keep pricing as legitimacy and now also unlock); ELECTION PUSH against an ally is legal and its exposure rung costs a lock-break with that ally. A crusher whose legitimacy is below threshold runs all Contested programs at half rate for 12 months, which is the bill Budapest sends to Rome and Reykjavik in the form the crusher feels. Yugoslavia 1948 (unlocked, NonAligned, Western aid verb open, Soviet TIGHTEN greyed 'NO GARRISON') and Finland (Neutralization lock) are the tutorial rows.

WHAT IT FEEDS. `alignment_of` consumers unchanged (bloc basing, patrons, red lines, nuclear ultimatum, masthead); ClientState clauses write position to the patron's band edge + lock for the truce term and Neutralization writes 0 + lock, so neutralized states exclude foreign basing with no new code, and `settlement::evaluate` prices dragging a +600 state into orbit dearer than a +100 one; released occupation zones flow zone.alignment/10 into the country position through the holder's bloc frame (holder-relative conversion, never a shared unit); `Domain::Political` penetration gets its first consumer; the victory checkpoint reads `Checkpoints`; crisis flashpoints reading alignment (Turkey Straits only while TUR is not Eastern) is the cheapest pillar-1 consumer and is deferred one step. Digest: Influence, Checkpoints and Intel added to the replay digest.

Defer the Government/Army/Street triad to v1.5 behind a written decision test: it ships only when a specific decision (arming an army in a party-state buys a future coup, not today's alignment; a jailed communist party under an Eastern-armed army) cannot be expressed by axis + stability + army_patron. Never the four-lean or per-region street model.

The fun skeptic calls windows-only 'dead air' in a real-time hourly sim; the history skeptic calls stochastic windows a spine-breaker.

Scripted window outcomes stay the default (band-edge shove) where nobody spent; a seeded roll happens only where a bloc has committed.

Without a street seat in v1, an election is a bounded seeded roll biased by programs and pushes that changes the band only if it clears the hysteresis gate; when the triad ships, the hostile pole governs only if its street share clears a stability-scaled majority gate. This is also what makes a +/-60 push meaningful: three points matter only near a threshold.

tensions.tension: Push vs pull: a monthly briefing card with one templated recommendation (legibility) vs pull-only decisions (espionage house rule); the fun skeptic says a correct recommendation plays the game and an incorrect one is noise.
tensions.recommendation: Keep the briefing card's facts (standings strip, three nearest contests with NEXT dates, COMMITMENTS n/cap); drop the recommendation line. Reading the world is the skill the pillar sells.

tensions.tension: Crush mechanics: convert the satellite into an occupation zone held by the patron (domestic-mirror) vs price the existing event options with lock + legitimacy + stability (integration).
tensions.recommendation: Event options. Occupation zones are derived from wars and are holder-relative; a peacetime crush has no (holder, owner) key. The mirror is fully satisfiable with LockAlignment, GrantLegitimacy, tension and `crushed_count` on hungary-soviet-decision and its 1953 sibling.

tensions.tension: Battleground set: fixed ~12-15 per era (legibility) vs derived from weights and open windows (board-game, decolonization). The fun skeptic warns an Angola marker in 1965 leaks the timeline.
tensions.recommendation: A 1950-sourced base set of ~30 with TS values as the seed, plus any country with an open contested window or an election window within 6 months. No era-scheduled additions; the timeline's dates stay invisible until their data-declared announcement lead.

synthesis.first_hour_acid_test: Boot 1950-01-01 as the USA (UGS_NATION=USA, speed 3, ~a real minute per game-month with pauses). MINUTE 0-5: press the INFLUENCE map mode and read the world in under ten seconds: hatched Warsaw-bloc satellites and NATO members (locked from the seed table), Japan and West Germany solidly Western with basing intact, about a dozen battleground pips (Italy, France, Greece, Turkey, Iran, Egypt, Indonesia, Indochina, Guatemala, Korea among them), Yugoslavia unlocked and olive, Egypt and Iran outlined as contested. The March paper carries Greece's result. Iran's PRESSURES ledger shows 'US AID +50 (ANNOUNCED)' then 'US AID +10 (2ND MONTH)'. MINUTE 25-40: the Campaign of Truth event (20 Apr) opens the PRESENCE verb with a wire line; the Turkey election pull card arrives with an ELECTION PUSH offer showing a Kent-word ladder and the legend once in the footer; the player may act or ignore it and nothing nags. On 14 May the valve fires from the sourced calendar: 'TURKEY: DEMOCRAT PARTY WINS - ANKARA LEANS WEST, TREATY OFFERED' is the top wire line, showing an election can deepen alignment, not only threaten it. On 25 June Korea fires unchanged: KOR/PRK/JAP basing, patrons and client logic behave exactly as before (regression: the_korean_war_runs_its_historical_arc and player_can_stand_aside pass), and the tension jump closes Europe to coups with a visible 'CLOSED AT CRISIS: EUROPE' line on the coup card. PASS CRITERIA: (1) map readable in ten seconds; (2) at most four pillar-2 decisions in six months and no click that was not a decision — no upkeep, no renewal; (3) one attributed rival spend in the February paper; (4) one player-caused verdict change before June and no band change the player did not cause; (5) two hands-off runs and a save/replay with the three influence commands produce identical digests including Influence, Checkpoints and Intel; (6) the_world_turns_to_1970 still passes with Cuba Eastern by 1965 and the new anchor snapshots within tolerance (every 1950 locked country still in band at 1955; at most three anchor-country band mismatches at 1960 hands-off); (7) the player can name one country they moved, one they are losing and why, and one contest they are saving a slot for, having opened no more than three documents.
sequencing: Attribution three-state machine (UNATTRIBUTED -> SUSPECTED -> PROVEN by named evidence objects) plus a pretext API in crisis.rs, shared with espionage v1.5; coup and election ladders then gain the FLIP WITH EVIDENCE and PROVEN-backfire rungs, and crisis flashpoints read alignment/patrons (Turkey Straits only while TUR is not Eastern).

AI covert participation: abstracted AI ELECTION PUSH and AI coup sponsorship in eligible battleground countries driven by the same published allocator (budget, not network), so the rival owns fast verbs and the contest is two-sided; legible via the chequebook line, with the bait multiplier still excluded.

The Government / Army / Street triad with a regime valve (Democracy{next_election} / PartyState / Military), threshold-rule elections reading the street seat, and the Peking-line marker after open-split-1961 — shipped only when the written decision test shows a decision the axis + stability + army_patron flag cannot express.

The Aswan auction: aid bids as placed projects from the construction pool with a recipient decision rule (which bid wins, when it leaks, when advisers are expelled), rival bids seen through political intel, and NAM actor verbs (solicit bids, host a conference, refuse a base) for playable India, Yugoslavia and Egypt — the answer to 'active attractor' as an actor.

Metropole as a distinct bidder: UK/France pillar-2 verbs (defence agreements, Community/Commonwealth locks, a reversal decision authored as a data default with a deadline), and the PRC as a third allocator pole after the split.

The sourced election calendar extended beyond battlegrounds, cadre pipelines (scholarships, officer training, volunteers) as a cheap invisible program with a 5-10 year payout landing on the next transition, and per-region street lean folded from occupation overlays.
UNGA annual session as a second scoring surface with issue-tagged resolutions, a membership table (60 -> 117) and a 90-day vote-swing window, read by era checkpoints alongside standings.

Systems-competition term: the living-standard differential as a checkpoint score line and a slow modifier on Presence rates in open societies — never a free monthly map mover — once the calibration harness can show it does not repaint the hands-off Third World.

open_questions_answered.question: Is Non-Aligned a passive middle or an active third attractor (Nehru/Tito/Nasser as a playable-ish force)?
open_questions_answered.answer: An active attractor in the design, implemented in two steps. History is unambiguous that it was active: Bandung (18-24 Apr 1955, 29 states) and Belgrade (1-6 Sep 1961, 25 states) were recruiting events; Nasser, Nehru, Tito, Sukarno, Nkrumah and Toure auctioned alignment and jailed the first bloc's local party; of the eight largest Soviet aid recipients of 1955-65 none became a satellite; the superpowers' best outcomes among them were denials. But no shipped game made NAM a third AI without a bespoke win condition (QMG: Cold War), and every 'field' proposal turns into decay the player merely fights. So: v1 models Non-Aligned as a FIELD WITH A SCORE — the passive middle falls out of hysteresis (denial cheaper than acquisition), the Bandung and Belgrade events (already in the corpus) add a monthly pull toward 0 in unlocked states adjacent to named champions (IND, EGY, YUG, IDN, later GHA) and grant those hosts legitimacy, NonAligned resolutions carry the highest inertia (half-rate movement, a transition required to leave), and checkpoints score 'denied' so both blocs have a reason to keep a state out of the other column. v1.5 makes it an ACTOR for playable middle powers: solicit bids, leak one bloc's offer to the other, host a conference, refuse a base, expel advisers — the auction — with the same slot budget a middle power already has. Never a third AI player.

open_questions_answered.question: Granularity: alignment per-country only, or per-faction within countries (army, church, unions) that covert ops can target individually?
open_questions_answered.answer: Per-country in v1, per-faction as a fixed triad in v1.5, never a per-country list. Four analysts converge on 'three factions' (Government / Army / Street with church, unions, parties and students as texture inside Street) and the historical record supports it — Egypt 1959 (Eastern arms, non-aligned leader, jailed communists, Western grain) cannot be one enum — but each analyst ships a different triad, none of the seeds exist for 226 + 37 countries, and both skeptics show a drift simulator of 678+ integers unless every seat changes a decision. So v1 stores one signed position plus dynamic stability plus an `army_patron` flag (whose equipment lineage the army runs on), which is enough to make the four verbs distinct: aid and presence move the position, election push acts at a dated window, coup sponsorship requires stability below the gate and an army not patronised by the rival, and arms grants set the flag. The triad ships in v1.5 behind a written decision test: it must express a decision the axis + stability + flag cannot (arming a party-state's army buys a future coup, not today's alignment; a street that turns against a locked government produces a rising with no valve; an election resolved by coalition threshold rather than average). Covert ops then target one seat each: arms -> Army, party funding -> Street, aid -> Government. Church, unions, students and parties are labels printed on the Street line, not state.
